title: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for that run. A follow-up rerun clears the printed backend as well.

Without the sibling edit, A→B→A can keep UI and backend aligned at `"input 2"`. Either interpretation of leftover keys should keep UI and printed state in sync; the #3512 unmount rule for an already-registered `persist_state=None` widget is that both sides reset in the same run.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current develop / #17106
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright)

### Additional Information

Found during QA of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17106#issuecomment-5813147965.

Related:

- #3512 — unmount should reset both the widget UI and the Python value in the same run
- #17093 / #17106 — delayed first mount after a leftover pre-registration user key (out of scope here)
- #12880 — identity-by-key (out of scope)

comments_data.body: Closing this, still evaluating the issue.

title: st.button lost callback from a fragment > dialog > fragment
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hello, since version 1.64 (previous was 1.59.2)

Some buttons doesn't get rerun in a setup with multiple layers of fragment.

fragment > dialog > fragment.

It was working on 1.59.2.
Is it expected ? should I test with a fragment key ?

Thank you

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import sys

import streamlit as st
from streamlit import runtime, session_state
from streamlit.web import cli as stcli

_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX = "_counter_value"


@st.fragment
def _render_button_in_dialog(page_key: str) -> None:
    """Fragment: increment button rendered inside the dialog."""
    counter_key = f"{page_key}{_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX}"
    st.metric("Count", session_state[counter_key])
    if st.button("➕ Increment", key=f"{page_key}_increment_btn", type="primary"):
        session_state[counter_key] += 1
        st.rerun(scope="fragment")


@st.fragment
def _render_button(page_key: str) -> None:
    """Fragment: open-dialog button."""
    counter_key = f"{page_key}{_COUNTER_KEY_SUFFIX}"

    if counter_key not in session_state:
        session_state[counter_key] = 0

    @st.dialog("Counter", width="small")
    def _open_dialog() -> None:
        _render_button_in_dialog(page_key)

    st.button("🔢 Open Counter", key=f"{page_key}_open_btn", on_click=_open_dialog)


def launch(page_key: str = "counter") -> None:
    _render_button(page_key)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if runtime.exists():
        st.set_page_config(layout="centered", page_title="Counter Demo", page_icon="🔢")
        launch(page_key="standalone")
    else:
        sys.argv = ["streamlit", "run", sys.argv[0]]
        sys.exit(stcli.main())
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

label should increment. rerun or callback triggered

### Current Behavior

no callback or rerun, button action is dropped.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

comments_data.body: I was able to reproduce this here: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-17112

This is a regression in the `fragment → dialog → fragment` nesting: the Increment button stays visible, but its click never reruns the inner fragment. `@st.dialog` is itself a `_fragment`. The repro opens that dialog from a fragment widget’s `on_click`, so the dialog (and the nested `@st.fragment` inside it) are registered during the callback. Since #16141 (in 1.64), callbacks bind `ThreadState.fragment_id` to the opener widget’s fragment, so those dialog/inner fragments become **descendants of the opener**. The opener then still does its default fragment rerun without calling the dialog again; `clear_stale_descendants` evicts the nested callables while the modal remains on `event_dg`. Later clicks send the evicted id and `AppSession.request_rerun` drops them. In 1.59.2 callbacks did not set `fragment_id`, so the dialog was registered as a root fragment and survived. A fragment `key` would not fix this. [#17039](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17039) (full-app-scoped dialog lifetime) likely covers this on `develop`, but its e2e opens the dialog from `if st.button()` rather than `on_click`, so that path should still be verified.

### Related Issues

- [#17011](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17011) — Same eviction class: a dialog opened from a fragment stays on screen after the parent fragment reruns, but clicks stop working. Closed by #17039; this report is the `on_click` + nested inner fragment variant.
- [#8591](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8591) — Opening a dialog from a button `on_click` historically made later dialog button clicks fail with a missing fragment id. Same callback-open pattern, without the extra inner `@st.fragment`.
- [#10283](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10283) — `st.dialog` inside `@st.fragment` has inconsistent lifecycle (dismiss/reopen) compared with a top-level dialog. Same feature intersection, different failure mode.

title: [Bug] st.dataframe() / st.table() silently kill WebSocket when DataFrame has non-ASCII column names + emoji data (no traceback, session loss)
body:
## Summary

`st.dataframe()` and `st.table()` silently close the WebSocket connection when the DataFrame contains **non-ASCII column names** (e.g. `ç`, `ê`, `/`) **combined with emoji in cell data**. No Python exception is raised, no error appears in the terminal — the browser simply reconnects with a brand-new session, wiping `st.session_state` entirely.

This is one of the hardest bugs to debug in Streamlit because it produces **zero tracebacks** and presents itself as an unrelated UX problem ("users keep getting logged out").

---

## Versions

| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| streamlit | 1.41.0 |
| pandas | 2.2.3 |
| Python | 3.11 |
| OS | Linux (Docker, python:3.11-slim) |

---

## Minimal Reproduction

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# This persists fine
if "logged_in" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["logged_in"] = False

if not st.session_state["logged_in"]:
    if st.button("Login"):
        st.session_state["logged_in"] = True
        st.rerun()
    st.stop()

st.write("✅ Logged in — session_state alive")

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Serviço": ["Manutenção Website", "Hospedagem"],   # ← non-ASCII column name (cedilha)
    "Valor/mês": ["R$ 100,00", "R$ 200,00"],           # ← non-ASCII + slash in column name  
    "Status": ["🟢 Ativo", "🔴 Pausado"],              # ← emoji in cell data
})

st.dataframe(df)   # 💥 WebSocket dies here — no exception raised
st.write("This line never renders — session is already dead")
```

Run with Docker:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install streamlit==1.41.0 pandas==2.2.3
COPY app.py .
ENTRYPOINT ["streamlit", "run", "app.py", "--server.headless=true", "--server.fileWatcherType=none"]
```

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Build and run the container
2. Open `http://localhost:8501`
3. Click "Login" → session is alive (`session_state["logged_in"] = True`)
4. `st.dataframe(df)` renders (or tries to)
5. Browser reconnects → `session_state` is empty → "Login" button appears again

---

## Observed Behavior

- `st.dataframe(df)` call executes without raising any Python exception
- The line after `st.dataframe()` **never executes** (confirmed via `print()` to stdout)
- Browser-side: WebSocket closes and immediately reconnects with a fresh session
- `st.session_state` is wiped clean — any auth/navigation state is lost
- **Identical behavior with `st.table(df)`** — same root cause

### Diagnostic method that revealed the bug

Since no traceback is produced, the only way to isolate it was:

1. Store a UUID in `session_state` on first load: `st.session_state["sid"] = uuid4()`
2. Display it on every render: `st.caption(f"sid: {st.session_state['sid']}")`
3. Add `print()` statements throughout the render function (visible in Docker logs)
4. The `print()` output stopped exactly at the `st.dataframe()` call
5. The displayed `sid` changed to a new value on the next render → confirmed new WebSocket session

---

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The bug appears to occur during **Arrow/protobuf serialization** of the DataFrame when:
- Column names contain multi-byte UTF-8 characters (`ç` = U+00E7, `ê` = U+00EA, `/` combined with accented chars)
- AND cell data contains 4-byte Unicode emoji (`🟢` = U+1F7E2, `🔴` = U+1F534)

The serialization fails at the **protocol level** (WebSocket frame), not at the Python level. The exception is caught internally by Streamlit/PyArrow and manifests as a connection close rather than an error message.

The bug does **not** occur when:
- Column names are ASCII-only
- Cell data has no emoji
- `st.write(df.to_dict(orient="records"))` is used instead (routes through JSON, not Arrow)

---

## Workaround

Replace `st.dataframe()` / `st.table()` with a **GFM markdown table** rendered via `st.markdown()`:

```python
def _esc(v) -> str:
    """Escape pipe to prevent breaking markdown table structure."""
    return str(v).replace("|", "\\|")

lines = [
    "| Servico | Valor_mes | Status |",
    "|---|---|---|",
]
for _, row in df.iterrows():
    lines.append(f"| {_esc(row['Serviço'])} | {_esc(row['Valor/mês'])} | {row['Status']} |")

st.markdown("\n".join(lines))
```

This bypasses the Arrow serialization layer entirely.

---

## Expected Behavior

- `st.dataframe()` should either render the DataFrame correctly OR raise a visible Python exception / display an in-app error
- The WebSocket connection should **never** be closed silently due to a data rendering issue
- If Arrow serialization fails, Streamlit should fall back to a JSON/HTML representation rather than terminating the session

---

## Additional Notes

- `fileWatcherType = "none"` was confirmed active — rules out hot-reload as the cause
- The Docker container did **not** restart (verified via log message count)
- The bug is **100% reproducible** in the described environment
- Changing column names to ASCII-only (`Servico`, `Valor_mes`) likely resolves the Arrow schema issue

Would appreciate confirmation of the root cause and whether a fix is planned for 1.41.x or 1.42.0.

comments_data.body:
This is a backend bug: `st.dataframe()` / `st.table()` with non-ASCII column names plus emoji cell values reportedly abort the script with no Python traceback, the WebSocket reconnects, and `st.session_state` is wiped. The reporter is on Streamlit 1.41.0 in Docker (`python:3.11-slim`).

The likely failure is inside pandas→Arrow conversion (`convert_pandas_df_to_arrow_bytes` → `pa.Table.from_pandas` in `lib/streamlit/dataframe_util.py`), not a WebSocket UTF-8 frame problem. Arrow IPC is sent as a protobuf `bytes` field (`ArrowData.data`), so a protocol-level text-frame encoding error would not stop the line after `st.dataframe()` from running. `print()` never executing matches a native crash/abort (or hang) in PyArrow that Streamlit cannot catch: conversion retries only handle `ArrowTypeError` / `ArrowInvalid` / `ArrowNotImplementedError` / `OverflowError`. Session wipe is the normal result of an unclean reconnect creating a new session. This was reported on 1.41.0; it should be re-checked on current Streamlit before treating it as still open.

### Related Issues

- [#16111](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16111) — Closest match: `st.dataframe` / `st.table` killed the process with a PyArrow `convert_column` SIGSEGV and no Python exception. Confirmed as upstream pyarrow 25.0.0 (different version/trigger than this 1.41.0 unicode+emoji report, same silent-failure class).
- [#9380](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9380) — Arrow serialization of certain column types fails inside the same conversion path; Streamlit should surface a conversion error instead of failing opaquely.
- [#8901](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8901) — Unclean WebSocket close currently starts a new session instead of restoring the old one, which is why this crash presents as users being “logged out.”

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Hi [USER], 

I haven't been able to reproduce your issue -- I am wondering if it might be caused by some failure other than the emoji/ascii issue that is specific to your environment -- or maybe some issue with emoji/ascii that is exasperated in your environment but not mine. I made a repro app here: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-16914

We did have an issue where a disconnect and reconnect was unclean and resulted in the app restarting that was fixed here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15909

Could you maybe try upgrading to at least 1.61 to see if this helps your issue with the reconnect starting a new session and wiping session state? 

I am also looking into improving the logging an debugability for this area.

Hi [USER], thank you for looking into this!

We were running **Streamlit 1.41.0**, which is well below the 1.61 threshold you mentioned. The fix referenced in #15909 (unclean reconnect causing a new session instead of resuming the existing one) matches our symptom exactly — every navigation to the MRR page wiped `session_state` and forced re-authentication.

Our workaround was replacing `st.dataframe()` with a `st.markdown()` GFM table, which stopped triggering the reconnect. In hindsight, the dataframe call was likely just the trigger that exposed the unclean reconnect behavior present in 1.41.0 — not the root cause itself.

We'll upgrade to ≥ 1.61 and report back whether `st.dataframe()` works correctly after the upgrade. If it does, it confirms #15909 as the underlying fix.

Thanks again for the pointer and for improving the logging/debuggability in this area — that would have saved us significant debugging time.

[USER] great, yeah, it doesn't seem like a reconnect should be triggered by this -- and it isn't in the rerpro app that I made -- but it's unclear to me why that is happening since I haven't reproduced it. But with the mentioned fix at least you should not be impacted by the reconnect in this way.

**Testing results on 1.63.0 — two separate bugs, one fixed, one still present**

We upgraded from 1.41.0 to 1.63.0 (following [USER]'s suggestion) and ran structured tests on both issues we had originally conflated into one. Results below.

---

**Bug 1 — Session loss on navigation (the original #15909): ✅ FIXED in 1.63.0**

We migrated from a single-page routing workaround (`session_state["pagina"]` + `on_click` callbacks) to native `st.navigation()` + `st.Page()` with callable functions. The session now survives navigation across all pages without any manual routing workaround.

One note for others hitting this: when using `st.Page()` with callable functions, Streamlit infers the URL path from `__name__`. If multiple pages share the same function name (e.g., all named `render`), you'll get a `StreamlitAPIException: Multiple Pages specified with URL pathname`. Fix: pass `url_path` explicitly to each `st.Page()`.

---

**Bug 2 — `st.dataframe()` with non-ASCII column names + emoji data: ❌ STILL PRESENT in 1.63.0**

We attempted to revert our `st.markdown()` GFM table workaround. As soon as `st.dataframe()` rendered with Portuguese column names (e.g., `"Descrição"`, `"Serviço"`) and emoji in cell values, the WebSocket disconnected silently — destroying `session_state` and sending the user back to login.

Side effect observed with `st.navigation()`: after the WebSocket reconnects, the framework renders the navigation sidebar before the auth `st.stop()` is reached, briefly exposing the page list to unauthenticated users. Not an auth bypass (page content is never served), but worth noting.

Our `st.markdown()` workaround remains in place for all data tables. We'll retest when the next Streamlit minor/major is released.

---

**Environment:** Python 3.11, Streamlit 1.63.0, Docker, Pandas 2.2.3, Plotly 5.24.1.

title: Deleting a widget's session_state key leaves the frontend showing the stale value (backend/frontend divergence for one rerun)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Deleting a keyed widget's entry from `st.session_state` (e.g. `del st.session_state["foo"]` inside a callback) does not reset the widget, but can lead to an inconsistency between frontend and backend.

The Python side returns the widget's *default* value for that run, but the frontend keeps displaying the old value, so backend and frontend disagree.

On the **next** rerun the backend silently re-adopts the stale frontend value, so the deletion is effectively undone.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

text = st.text_input("Foo", value="default", key="foo")

st.write("widget returned:", repr(text))

def populate():
    st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"

def delete():
    del st.session_state["foo"]

st.button("Populate", on_click=populate)
st.button("Delete", on_click=delete)
st.button("Noop")

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app.
2. Click **Populate** (callback sets `st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"`). The text input now shows `hello` and `widget returned: 'hello'`.
3. Click **Delete** (callback runs `del st.session_state["foo"]`).
4. Observe the text input on screen vs. the `widget returned:` line.
5. Click **Noop** (any interaction that triggers a plain rerun) and observe again.

### Expected Behavior

The widget value in the frontent and backend should be consistent. After deleting a widget's key in session state, it should presumably fall back to its default value.

### Current Behavior

- After clicking Delete, the backend returns `widget returned: "default''` , but the frontend widget still displays `"hello"`.
- After the next rerun (step 5), the backend re-adopts the stale frontend value, and both show `"hello"`.

### Screenshot

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.2
- Python version: 3.14.6
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chromium


### Additional Information

Likely related: #5442

comments_data.body:
Deleting a keyed widget's entry from `st.session_state` correctly clears backend state and makes the widget return its default for that run, but the frontend is never told to adopt that default. In `SessionState.register_widget`, `widget_value_changed` is only set for programmatic *sets* (`is_new_state_value`), bound/persisted restores, page-scoped drops, and disabled-value discards — not for key deletion. As a result the UI keeps the stale value, and the next rerun's `set_widgets_from_proto` re-imports that frontend value into session state, undoing the delete.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5442 — Near-duplicate (filed as enhancement): deleting a widget key resets the Python return value to the default but leaves the browser widget stuck on the previous selection; the next rerun re-syncs to the stale UI value.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10169 — Related frontend/backend divergence: pending widget edits can remain visible on the client while not being submitted to the backend after programmatic `st.rerun()` / `st.switch_page()`.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9082 — Related session-state/widget sync: widgets in conditional blocks fail to reflect values from `st.session_state` when remounted, another backend-vs-frontend state mismatch.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.5-high`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

I’d like to work on this. My proposed scope is to first add an `AppTest` regression covering deletion of a keyed widget from `st.session_state`, its immediate default value, and the following rerun. I would then update the widget-state synchronisation path so the reset value is sent back to the frontend without changing normal programmatic assignments or widget cleanup.

Before I start, should deleting a keyed widget always reset it to its declared default, or are there cases where removing the key should preserve the current frontend value?

title: format_func does not keep the pill selected when the pill's text changes.
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

In the first part of the code below, two interdependent "pills" components are created; the `format_func` adjusts the text displayed on the buttons to show the record count for each category.
When a category is selected in the first component, it updates the component below by filtering subcategories and changing the displayed text to reflect the record count for each subcategory.
However, when the category selection is cleared, the second component retains the value in `session_state` and the object's internal state, yet it does not visually appear selected, which misleads the user.
In this scenario, the subcategory component should appear selected, even though the displayed text has changed.

The second part uses the "same code" but without `format_func`: here, if you select a category, select a subcategory, and then deselect the category, the subcategory remains visually selected.


```
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {"id": 1, "name":"name a","category": "A","category_b": "D"},
            {"id": 2, "name":"name b","category": "A","category_b": "D"},
            {"id": 3, "name":"name c","category": "B","category_b": "D"},
            {"id": 4, "name":"name d","category": "B","category_b": "E"},
            {"id": 5, "name":"name e","category": "C","category_b": "E"},
            {"id": 6, "name":"name f","category": "C","category_b": "F"},
            {"id": 7, "name":"name g","category": "C","category_b": "F"},
            {"id": 8, "name":"name h","category": "C","category_b": "G"},
            {"id": 9, "name":"name i","category": "C","category_b": "G"},
            {"id": 10, "name":"name j","category": "C","category_b": "H"},
        
        ]
    
    )
df_2 = df.copy()

cat = st.pills("Category",df['category'].unique(),format_func= lambda x: f'{x} ({len(df.loc[df["category"] == x])})',key='category')
if cat:
    df = df.loc[df['category'] == cat]

catb = st.pills("Category B",df['category_b'].unique(),format_func= lambda x: f'{x} ({len(df.loc[df["category_b"] == x])})',key='category_b')
if catb:
    df = df.loc[df['category_b'] == catb]
st.code(cat)
st.code(catb)
st.dataframe(df)


cat2 = st.pills("Category",df_2['category'].unique(),key='category_2')
if cat2:
    df_2 = df_2.loc[df_2['category'] == cat2]

catb2 = st.pills("Category B",df_2['category_b'].unique(),key='category_b_2')
if catb2:
    df_2 = df_2.loc[df_2['category_b'] == catb2]
st.code(cat2)
st.code(catb2)
st.dataframe(df_2)

comments_data.body:
### Summary

This is a `st.pills` bug (also applies to `st.segmented_control`, which shares the same `ButtonGroup` implementation): when `format_func` output for the currently-selected option changes between reruns (here the record count in the label changes as `df` is filtered), the pill visually appears **deselected**, even though `session_state` and the return value still hold the correct underlying value. The reporter's second example without `format_func` works, isolating `format_func` as the trigger.

### Potential root cause

Since the 1.54 refactor, these button-group widgets identify/track the selected option by its **formatted display string** rather than by the underlying value:

- Frontend (`frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/ButtonGroup/ButtonGroup.tsx`) stores the widget value as the formatted content string and highlights selection via `contentStringsToIndices(options, value)`. When `format_func` output changes (e.g. `"D (2)"` → `"D (3)"`), the stored string no longer matches any current option's content, so `selectedKeys` is empty and nothing renders as selected.
- Backend (`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/button_group.py`) maps wire values via `formatted_option_to_option_index`, and only preserves the *value* through `session_state_fallback` — which is why `session_state`/the return value stay correct while the visual selection is lost.

Note there is already substantial handling for dynamic `format_func`/option changes in recent versions — the `session_state_fallback` + `set_value` re-serialization added in #15522 (shipped in 1.60.0) and the dynamic-options support in #13684. The report was filed without a version, so the team should confirm the exact Streamlit version and whether this still reproduces on the latest release; this may be a remaining edge case in the interdependent (parent→child) pills flow rather than a fully open regression.

### Related Issues

- [#12392](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12392) — State management issues with `st.pills` when options change dynamically based on a parent selection (selections get reset). Closest match: same widget and the same interdependent parent→child pattern.
- [#8008](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8008) — `st.selectbox` returns a stale value when `format_func` output changes; same root cause of using `format_func` output as the option identity/key.
- [#14115](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14115) — `st.radio` returns the wrong option because (since 1.54) options are identified by their formatted display text; same family of `format_func`-as-identity bugs.

# comp.py

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"
```

streamlit v 1.55

I'm trying to migrate our custom js widgets from v1 component api to the non-iframe v2 api.
It seems far more powerful, and seems like it'll cut boilerplate.
In our style, we have accumulated over the years a collection of js/client side running code, that doesn't particularly need/have an html or user-interfacing component.

I think I've noticed an issue, where values are getting returned from the js frontend (as seen by console.log msgs), but the streamlit backend logs see those msgs as dropped. I'm still getting the hang of the runtime behaviors of this new component api, to figure out how to update our v1 components, so I've been trying to test it. If this is not the expected or correct usage, I'm all ears, but I'm working my best from the online docs + repo src implementation. 

This is our current design / usage analysis of the v2 api:
- We declare/write a st.components.v2.component(...) object in a helper file, that will not be modified, with a unique name
- The js string includes all helper functions, and an `export default function(component: FrontendRendererArgs)`
- This default function is the per-widget-instantiation, and only run once (see below)
- It sets up callbacks or such on html elements
- If the component is called with a `key`, then all setTriggerValue and setStateValue items populate session_state
- Without an explicit `key`, setTriggerValue won't populate session_state, but the rest of the python arguments (data) are used to calculate a unique frontend key
- No two component instances therefore can have the exact same args (data)
- If the args to the component don't change, the widget object stays created, and is not re-instantiated
- If the rest of the args (data) to the component change, without a `key`, the old widget is discarded, and a new component is instantiated

Our goal is to have high-level code that uses caching & post processing of raw lower-level data call these low-level components as needed. But if the components are called, I expect them to behave consistently. 

In this particular example, the js component does (for example!!!) a failproof cookies query on instantiation and returns it via setTriggerValue.
```js
export default function (component){  component.setTriggerValue("get_cookies", document.cookie); }
```
We wrap that `st_comp_get_cookies: st.components.v2.component` in a helper function.
```python
def get_raw_cookies():
    obj = st_comp_get_cookies(data={"_": unique_line_time()})
```
If we feed `data` a value that's unique to the line (line traceback stack), the multiple calls of the widget will be unique even if fed the same other args. It would create a new component when there's a new/unique call (args or location), otherwise only instantiated once.
If we feed `data` a value that's unique in time, then every call is a new widget instance, and the js default function runs each time.

In the v1 api, when the app first loaded, the components wouldn't always respond right away. So I'd check if the returned value was empty or not.
```python
# get_raw_cookies()
if not isisntance(obj, dict) or "get_cookies" not in obj:
    # Very first run, component mightn't be ready
    time.sleep(initial_setup_sleep)
    st.rerun()
print(f"{obj["get_cookies"]=}")
```

Given the above files, with more logging added, I noticed a very strange behavior. (This is just a heavily reduced version of our real prod code; and I only chose documents.cookies because it _can't fail_).
In the browser console, everytime the page reloaded (hard reload F5, or soft rerun from some other input), the console logged the new widget instance, the cookie fetch, and that succeeded.
But in the python logs, sometimes it worked, sometimes it did not. 
With the "rerun if fail" check, if this was the only indeterminite execution, it'd work quickly enough, and then the rest of the code would execute.
But with multiple components doing this, it suddenly became impossible for both to work at the same time.
```python
get_raw_cookies() # Sometimes reruns, ok
get_raw_cookies() # Always reruns, when the above finally works
st.header("This never runs")
assert False
```

Sorry if this was rather long winded, but I'm either uncertain I'm understanding the runtime behaviors correctly, trying not to misrepresent our goals, possibly oblivious to a better v2 design, or just unaware of what to reasonably expect from this as for behavior.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Copy the 3 files
2. docker compose up (or, it's _really just_ python 3.10 and streamlit 1.55 in the env, nothing else)
3. Open browser to streamlit instance
4. Compare the browser logs, the python logs, and how the page doesn't load

### Expected Behavior

I expect at app start the component to fail, but afterwards I'd expect each new component creation to successfully be created, successfully transmit setState/TriggerValue back to the component, and get returned by the component, before the backend continues on. (Consistency / Determinism). (Otherwise, we'd design differently)

### Current Behavior

I've tried variations of the above files, such as adding more sleeps on python side, but the js side seems to be sending the values back, and the python side seems to inconsistently receive them. The first component ~1/2 the time, and the second always fails when the first doesn't.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Ubuntu
- Browser: Chromium / Opera

First, trigger values in the CCv2 API are only surfaced on the result object when you register a matching `on_<key>_change` callback ([docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/custom-components/components-v2/state-and-triggers#callback-registration)). This is a bug report about Components V2 (`st.components.v2.component`) dropping `setTriggerValue` (and `setStateValue`) results when the component's JavaScript runs on initialization (mount) rather than in response to user interaction. The root cause is a timing/race condition inherent in the Streamlit execution model: the Python script finishes execution before the frontend has a chance to render the component, load its JS module (async `import()`), execute the default function, and send the trigger/state value back via `updateWidgets`. This means the component always returns an empty/default result on its first script run. The problem compounds when multiple such components are used sequentially — satisfying one triggers a rerun that resets the other, making it effectively impossible for both to return values simultaneously. The issue discussion confirms this affects both `setTriggerValue` and `setStateValue` during mount-time initialization, and multiple community members have requested a "blocking" component mode that waits for the frontend JS to execute before the backend continues.

- [#8041 - Restart app if component doesn't load](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8041): Describes the same fundamental problem for v1 components — components not being ready on first load and needing a workaround (rerun/retry). The reporter specifically notes that Components V2 should help fix this, but as this issue shows, the same timing problem persists.
- [#13671 - Allow bytes in a dict for custom components v2](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13671): Related Components V2 enhancement for data serialization. Not a duplicate, but part of the same V2 API surface area being actively developed.
- [#9422 - `Streamlit.setComponentValue` doesn't return `Set` type variables](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9422): Related to data type handling in custom component return values. Different root cause but affects the same custom component value passing path.

[USER] [USER] I want to mention this feature we are testing as well [Allow programmatically writing cookies during a session](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14730), there is also a package available already that you could test to see if it meets your needs.

Did some more investigation around this issue. Short version: no messages are being lost in transit. Two separate by-design mechanisms produce what looks like dropping, and one genuine bug did fall out of the investigation, filed separately as #16732.

All measurements below are on 1.62.0:

### What reproduces

The reported symptom reproduces deterministically — the page never finishes loading, the second component never resolves, and the retry loop runs hot: **863 script runs in 15 seconds (~58 reruns/sec)**, with no error or warning surfaced.

### Why the original version never converges

`data` is hashed into the element id, so `unique_line_time()` builds a **different widget on almost every run**. The value the previous instance sent belongs to a widget that no longer exists. Measured: **0 of 1,271 runs** received a value, with 688 distinct element ids observed in 12 seconds. It works only when two runs happen to land in the same second — which is exactly the "about half the time" behaviour described above.

This is documented behaviour, in `component-v2-lib/src/types.ts`:

> If a component is mounted without a `key` parameter in Python, and one of the parameters in the mounting command changes, then this frontend key may change between app runs.

One consequence worth flagging, since avoiding `session_state` clutter was the stated reason for going unkeyed: the unkeyed version is the one that **accumulates** orphaned widget entries — registered ids grew 2 → 6 → 8 → 10 → 12 → 14 over six runs. Passing a `key` is what keeps state bounded.

### The trigger diagnosis in this thread was correct

The conclusion that trigger values are "resurfaced once, just... only resurfaced once", and the comparison to `if st.button("1") and st.button("2")`, is exactly right. `_reset_triggers()` in `runtime/state/session_state.py` nulls every trigger value at the end of each run. With stable `data` a component mounts once and sends once, so after that value is consumed there is nothing left to re-send — two sequential mount-time triggers deadlock. Measured: the second component received a value **0 times across 126 runs**.

### Three corrections to this thread

1. **Trigger values do not require an `on_<key>_change` callback.** Earlier in the thread we said the key wouldn't appear in the result without one; that isn't right. None of our repros registered a callback and values arrived normally — the pushback on that point was correct.
2. **The `st.stop()` approach doesn't work.** It loops forever exactly like `st.rerun()` — the second component still never resolves. Worth stating plainly since it was suggested here and looked promising.
3. **The automated triage comment above is only half right.** Async module loading does explain an empty result on the *first* run, but it predicts convergence on run 2 — which is what a stable-`data` component actually does. It doesn't explain the permanent failure.

### What works reliably

| Pattern | Result |
|---|---|
| `setStateValue` with a stable key | resolves in **2 runs** |
| Five `setStateValue` components at once | all resolve together in **2 runs** |
| `setStateValue` on mount, changing `data` | 21/21 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from an event handler | 40/40 delivered |
| Inside `@st.fragment` | works |
| Inside an `if st.button(...)` block | never resolves — matching the second report above |

### The one genuine bug

Separately from the above: `setTriggerValue` called **during mount** loses roughly a quarter of values when the component remounts on changed `data`, even with an explicit `key` and a verified-stable element id. Filed as #16732. Both alternatives above are unaffected, so the practical guidance is unchanged — use `setStateValue` for initialization values.

### What we're doing with this issue

Since the reported "result dropping" turns out to be documented behaviour plus the separately-filed bug, we're converting this issue to the enhancement underneath it — a supported way to await an initialization value without leaving permanent `session_state` entries — which is what's actually being asked for here.

[USER] [USER] — this is the part we'd need your input on to design it. At the point of the call, what needs to be guaranteed: that the value is *present*, or just a reliable way to distinguish "not ready yet" from "genuinely empty"? And what makes a persistent `session_state` entry unacceptable — the volume, the staleness, or key hygiene? The point that "supply a default" can't distinguish an expected value from cache invalidation is the crux, and knowing which of those matters would shape the answer.

title: container.empty() not explicitly clearing when refreshes/streaming data is needed via st.rerun()
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Not entirely sure if this is considered a bug or would require a feature request, please redirect if necessary:

When building a UI that polls or streams updates using `st.rerun()`, containers that previously rendered content can become stale instead of clearing, even when they have stable keys and `container.empty()` is explicitly called.

In our case we render rows into pre-created keyed containers (attempting to prevent layout artifacts). When a row is removed:
	•	the item is removed from `session_state`
	•	`row_container.empty()` is called
	•	the script reruns (due to polling)

Instead of disappearing immediately, the container’s previous contents linger briefly (“pulse”) and behave like stale elements until Streamlit finishes the rerun cycle.

This occurs even when:
	•	containers have stable keys
	•	nested container trees exist
	•	`.empty()` is explicitly called
	•	the layout structure remains stable between reruns

### Reproducible Code Example

[[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-14280)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time
import uuid

# --------------------------------------------
# Session state
# --------------------------------------------

if "items" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["items"] = [str(uuid.uuid4())[:5] for _ in range(5)]

# --------------------------------------------
# Stable row containers
# --------------------------------------------

row_containers = []
MAX_ROWS = 5
for i in range(MAX_ROWS):
    row_containers.append(
        st.container(key=f"row_container_{i}")
    )

# Additional nested containers (each with its own key) to demonstrate that
# having stable keyed containers does not prevent clearing
row_content_containers = []
for i in range(MAX_ROWS):
    row_content_containers.append(
        st.container(key=f"row_content_container_{i}")
    )


# --------------------------------------------
# Render rows in their stable containers
# --------------------------------------------

for idx, item in enumerate(st.session_state["items"]):

    # Get the stable container for this row index
    container = row_containers[idx]

    # A nested tree of elements to stress diffing
    container.markdown(f"### Row {idx} — {item}")
    container.code(item)

    if container.button("Remove", key=f"remove_{item}"):
        # Attempt to remove row
        st.session_state["items"] = [
            x for x in st.session_state["items"] if x != item
        ]

        # Explicitly clear the row container
        row_containers[idx].empty()
        st.rerun()


# --------------------------------------------
# Polling simulation, usually we'd grab new data here and update session state, but for this demo we just refresh
# --------------------------------------------
st.caption("Polling refresh…")
time.sleep(2)
st.rerun()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Delete any of the "items" shown in the UI, they will stale but never actually clear unless we stopped refreshing/polling. 

### Expected Behavior

Explicitly cleared containers disappear immediately with all their contents. Rather than relying on "is this missing?" type calculations after script completion.

### Current Behavior

Container contents just go stale and pulse in and out.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.54.0

### Additional Information

_No response_

comments_data.body:
This issue reports that calling `container.empty()` followed by `st.rerun()` does not immediately clear the container's contents on the frontend. Instead, the old elements linger as "stale" (greyed-out) elements until the next script run fully completes. The root cause is in how Streamlit's render tree works: when a new script run begins, keyed containers inherit their children from the previous run (see `addBlock` in `AppRoot.ts`). These inherited children are marked as stale (via `isElementStale` in `Block/utils.ts`) and rendered with reduced opacity, but they are only actually removed from the tree when `clearStaleNodes` is called at the **end** of the script run. In the reporter's case, a `time.sleep(2)` polling loop means stale elements remain visible for the full duration of each run, causing a "pulsing" effect. The `container.empty()` call from the previous run has no lasting effect since the container is re-created with inherited children in the new run.

### Related Issues

- **#12069** — [st.empty does not clear removed elements](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12069): Very likely a duplicate. Reports the same core behavior where `st.empty()` containers fail to clear old elements if new content has fewer items, leaving ghost elements visible. Confirmed bug, P3.
- **#10126** — [`st.close()` or `st.end()` to remove stale elements mid-run](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10126): A feature request that directly addresses the underlying limitation. Proposes a mechanism to explicitly discard remaining stale elements within a container before the script run finishes, which would solve this issue.
- **#5044** — [empty() does not remove cleared elements?](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5044): A long-standing related bug where `.empty()` clears the UI but doesn't fully remove internal widget state, leading to DuplicateWidgetID errors. Confirmed bug, P3.

I would recommend to either put the auto-updating UI into a fragment with `run_every` or use `streamlit-autorefresh`:  https://github.com/kmcgrady/streamlit-autorefresh Does this work for your case?

### Summary

When using the newly introduced option to provide a callable as data argument, the callable runs without ScriptRunContext.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# app.py
import csv
import io

import streamlit as st

    foo = st.session_state.get("foo", "nope")
    print(foo)

    writer = csv.writer(buffer)

    return buffer.getvalue()


st.download_button(
    label="Download",

    file_name="foo.csv",

)

st.session_state["foo"] = "bar"
```

2. Click the button

Raises Thread 'asyncio_0': missing ScriptRunContext! This warning can be ignored when running in bare mode.

### Expected Behavior

When called from the download_button, the function `to_csv` should have context, and see the currenct `session_state`.

### Current Behavior

Warning
```
Thread 'asyncio_0': missing ScriptRunContext! This warning can be ignored when running in bare mode.
```

comments_data.body:
Somehow I missed this issue https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13337
Closing as duplicate

Confirming this from a production incident — and it's a bit worse than "missing ScriptRunContext produces a warning": inside that thread, `st.session_state` reads return stale values and `@st.cache_data`-wrapped calls silently return whatever was already cached, **with no error and no warning**. Both just look like they worked.

Our incident: a `data=callable` on `st.download_button` called into functions that (transitively) read `@st.cache_data`-cached helpers. Because those calls run outside `ScriptRunContext`, they picked up cached results from a *different* request context — users occasionally downloaded a file that didn't match what they'd just generated on screen, with nothing in the logs to explain why. We only found the mechanism by tracing the full call graph of the callable, not just inspecting it — a lambda that looks pure can still be unsafe if anything it calls touches cached/session state indirectly.

We ended up moving off lazy `data=` entirely (eager bytes, pre-warmed at save time) because we couldn't make the callable's dependency tree provably free of session/cache reads. For anyone hitting this: if your callable calls anything that isn't a pure function of its arguments, the missing context isn't just a perf/warning issue, it's a correctness one.

comments_data.body: Hey [USER] thanks for filing this issue. This is tough for us to debug on our side. You might need to debug with `authlib` as this is where the error is coming from. We'll keep this open in case anyone else runs into it.
This might be the same thing as https://github.com/authlib/authlib/issues/699?

This issue reports a failure when authenticating against Microsoft Entra ID (MSAL) using `st.login`. The error `AADSTS900144: The request body must contain the following parameter: 'client_id'` occurs during the OAuth token exchange step. This is likely caused by a mismatch in the token endpoint authentication method - Microsoft Azure AD requires the `client_id` to be sent in the request body (`client_secret_post` method), but authlib may be sending it via HTTP Basic Auth header (`client_secret_basic` method) by default.

The Streamlit maintainers have already identified this as potentially related to an upstream authlib issue (authlib/authlib#699). A possible workaround is to add `token_endpoint_auth_method = "client_secret_post"` to the client configuration, though this may need to be done via `client_kwargs` in the secrets configuration.

### Related Issues

- **#11391** - [Cannot use common tenant with microsoft login: InvalidClaimError](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11391) - Another Microsoft/authlib authentication issue where the "common" tenant fails with an invalid claim error. Both issues highlight challenges with Microsoft Entra ID integration through authlib.

- **#10707** - [New client_kwargs entry (acr_values) is not accepted, auth fails](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10707) - Related issue where custom OAuth parameters in `client_kwargs` are not being properly passed to the authentication flow, which may be relevant if the workaround requires setting `token_endpoint_auth_method`.

- **#10160** - [Expose OAuth errors during st.login](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10160) - Enhancement request to better expose OAuth errors, which would help users debug issues like this one.

title: Regression (1.50.0): widget value no longer updates when dependent on another widget
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In previous versions, a widget with a key could update its value dynamically based on another widget. For example, a `st.text_area` would change when the selection in a `st.selectbox` changed.

In 1.50.0, this no longer works. If a widget has a `key`, its `value` only reflects the initial `value` provided. Changes in other widgets no longer update it automatically.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

sys_dict = {"key1": "value1", "key2": "value2"}

selected_key = st.selectbox(
    "Key:",
    options=list(sys_dict.keys()),
    key="selected_key",
)

selected_value = st.text_area(
    "Value:",
    value=sys_dict[selected_key],  # depends on selectbox
    height=150,
    key="selected_value",
)

st.write(f"state.selected_key: {st.session_state.selected_key}")
st.write(f"state.selected_value: {st.session_state.selected_value}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run above code using 1.49.1
2. Observe that changes to the selectbox change the value in the text_area/session_state
3. Upgrade to 1.50.0
4. Observe that changes to the selectbox do not change the value in the text_area/session_state

### Expected Behavior

- If selected_key == "key1", the text_area shows "value1".
- If selected_key == "key2", the text_area shows "value2".

Switching the selectbox causes the text_area to update accordingly.

### Current Behavior

On the first render, the text_area shows the correct value.
After that, changing the selectbox does not update the text_area.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.50.0
- Python version: 3.11.13
- Operating System: MacOS
- Browser: Firefox

comments_data.body: I suspect this is down to #12397 and maybe the new expected behaviour?

Yes, e.g text input value doesn't update on initial run or reruns even if input is entered yet, and value='foo', foo is not updated in text input.....this is true when widget has set key, otherwise foo is updated, there seems no use of value parameter if key is used in widgets
On first run, widgets with key parameter set, widget value is updated in session state as empty and there is no effect of value parameter

Hm, it seems like this is expected given #11277, and from the issue description that we were ok with making this change even knowing that this would end up changing the behavior for some use cases.

I'm guessing that the idea was that we're knowingly bending the rules by making a breaking change here but were willing to do so assuming that the number of bugs/weird cases fixed by the behavior would outweigh the ones we'd create.

CCing [USER] / [USER] to keep an eye on the effects of #11277, though.

The change is expected as part of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11277. The `value` parameter was always meant to be just the default value. It was just a "lucky" coincidence that you could use it previously to update the widget value, since it always caused the frontend component to be reinitialised. This is something we are changing when `key` is set (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11277). The workaround is to either remove the `key` parameter or to set the widget value via the session state (the official way to programmatically update the state): `st.session_state["my_widget_key"] = "foo"`.

We are keeping this issue open to collect more feedback on this change.

> The workaround is to either remove the `key` parameter or to set the widget value via the session state (the official way to programmatically update the state): `st.session_state["my_widget_key"] = "foo"`.

I misunderstood this at first, it took some stabbing to confirm the intended behavior: 

When instantiating one of these widgets, you should set `key` **OR** `value`, but not both.

You can, however, pre-set the value of `my_widget_key` in st.session_state  **before** instantiating the widget to get a default value (was this historically the case, or is this a coordinating change? I feel like this used to raise an error), **but** if you pass in a key at all, the `value` parameter is silently ignored. It may be worth a emitting a warning if both of these parameters are set.

> The change is expected as part of [#11277](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11277). The `value` parameter was always meant to be just the default value. It was just a "lucky" coincidence that you could use it previously to update the widget value, since it always caused the frontend component to be reinitialised. This is something we are changing when `key` is set ([#11277](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11277)). The workaround is to either remove the `key` parameter or to set the widget value via the session state (the official way to programmatically update the state): `st.session_state["my_widget_key"] = "foo"`.
> 
> We are keeping this issue open to collect more feedback on this change.


This is good. It's just not as concise as it used to be.

This broke my app badly. I had designed an elaborate finance planning app.

So my use-case is this: 
1. SelectBox --> To select a scenario (e.g. of scenarios -> Scenario 1: No new asset openings, Scenario 2: Asset openings same as last year, Scenario 3: 30% more assets than previous year after July 2026 etc..)
2. A slew of widgets, one each for a forecasted month, change as per the selection in the SelectBox
3. The user can also manually specify values in the slew of widgets..

Now, I cannot realize my use-case now in the new scheme of things.
Please educate me on how to handle this scenario.
Thanks!

**UPDATE**
I worked around the issue after a lot of headache.
1. I created a "_twin" session state that mirrors the session_state value of the widget. I created a wrapper over the selectbox function to create and maintain this _twin variable
2. The _twin variable enables me to tell whether the current streamlit run was triggered due to a change in the widget (or) due to change of something else. The same is reported as an additional return value from the selectbox() wrapper.
3. I save the change variables of important selectboxes I care about for a particular widget
4. Using the "change" state and the "_twin" state --> I decide to write or not to write into st.session_state variable of the widget before rendering the widget.

title: Multiselect Visual State vs Returned Value Mismatch
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

After `st.rerun()` following cache clear, sidebar multiselect shows one selection visually but returns different values to the code.

### Reproducible Code Example

[[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-12305)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# Cached data function that returns test data
@st.cache_data
def load_test_data():
    return pd.DataFrame({
        'id': ['item_1', 'item_2', 'item_3'],
        'type': ['TypeA', 'TypeB', 'TypeC'],
        'value': [100, 200, 300]
    })

st.title("Multiselect Bug Reproducer")

# Sidebar with reload button (matching original pattern)
with st.sidebar:
    st.header("Data Management")
    if st.button("🔄 Reload Data", help="Clear cache and reload"):
        load_test_data.clear()
        st.success("Cache cleared! Data will be reloaded.")
        st.rerun()

# Load data
df = load_test_data()

# Extract unique types (matching original pattern)
all_types = sorted(df['type'].dropna().unique())

# Sidebar filters (matching original pattern)
st.sidebar.header("Filters") 

# Create multiselect in sidebar with all types as default
selected_types = st.sidebar.multiselect(
    "Select Types",
    all_types,
    default=all_types,  # All selected by default
)

# Filter data based on selection
filtered_df = df.copy()
if selected_types:
    filtered_df = filtered_df[filtered_df['type'].isin(selected_types)]

# Show debug info that reveals the bug
st.write("### Debug Information:")
st.write(f"**Multiselect shows selected**: {selected_types}")
st.write(f"**Filtered data rows**: {len(filtered_df)}")
st.write(f"**Item IDs in filtered data**: {sorted(filtered_df['id'].tolist())}")

st.write("---")
st.write("### Steps to reproduce bug:")
st.write("1. Initially all types are selected → shows 3 rows")
st.write("2. **In sidebar, deselect 'TypeA'** → should show 2 rows")
st.write("3. **Click 'Reload Data' button in sidebar**")
st.write("4. **BUG**: Sidebar shows 'TypeB, TypeC' but filtered data includes all 3 rows")

st.write("### Show actual data:")
st.dataframe(filtered_df)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Put the above in `reproducer.py` and run
2. Deselect "TypeA" in sidebar (UI shows "TypeB, TypeC" selected)
3. Click "🔄 Reload Data" button in sidebar
4. **BUG**: UI still shows "TypeB, TypeC" but code receives `['TypeA', 'TypeB', 'TypeC']`


### Expected Behavior

Multiselect returns what it shows visually.

### Current Behavior

- Visual: Shows "TypeB, TypeC" ✅
- Returned: `['TypeA', 'TypeB', 'TypeC']` ❌


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.45.1
- Python version: 3.12.1
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

I originally discussed this [here]( https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/clearing-cache-on-a-single-method-screws-up-multiselect-selected-items/119093) and it looks like [this discussion](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/multipage-with-multiselect-default-and-session-state/52619) may also be relevant. 

  Related GitHub Issues:
  - Issue #6079: "session_state not actually changed until second page reload" - Documents that session_state doesn't update immediately after widget interaction, requiring double reloads
  - Issue #4223: "Issue in multiselect - default and current value overlap" - Reports similar problems where default parameters conflict with current selections in multiselect widgets
  - Issue #4695: "multiselect reset to defaults behavior is inconsistent" - Documents inconsistent behavior when multiselect widgets reset to defaults during reruns

comments_data.body:
[USER] Thanks for reporting this issue. I reproduced it [here](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-12305). The behaviour you are seeing is annoying but currently expected. This is caused by the `st.rerun()` being used in the middle of the script -> which causes the following widgets not being rendered for one rerun -> which causes the widget state to be cleaned up. 

There is a workaround for this by using a placeholder and checking the button click at the end of the script (or saving the click value and running rerun at the end of the rerun), e.g.:

````python
# Sidebar with reload button (matching original pattern)
with st.sidebar:
    st.header("Data Management")
    reloade_button_container = st.container()

# Rest of the app....

with reloade_button_container:
    if st.button("🔄 Reload Data", help="Clear cache and reload"):
        load_test_data.clear()
        st.success("Cache cleared! Data will be reloaded.")
        st.rerun()
````

Closing this issue since we have a feature request to provide a way to keep the widget state even when a widget isn't rendered for a rerun: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6074 Feel free to upvote and engage on this feature request.

title: Concurrency issues with `st.data_editor` `on_change` callback: Using the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` leads to multiple processing or potential data loss
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

**Issue Description:**

When a user edits cells in the `st.data_editor` object, the `on_change` callback function is triggered. If the user makes additional edits while the `on_change` callback is still running, some edits are processed multiple times (in this case, twice for edits of the first interaction and once for the second interaction) when using the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` to process the user edits. This occurs because the callback is threaded, and the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` object still includes the edits from the previous user interaction.

**Additional Issue:**

Attempting to fix this revealed another issue: If the `on_change` callback for a previous call takes longer to execute than the latest call, the Streamlit page reloads before the previous `on_change` callbacks are finished. As a result, not all cells of the `st.data_editor` object are updated, leading to potential loss of user edits. This seems to be fixed by using `threading.Lock()` in the on_change callback function.

**Request:**
I found a solution to this, but would like to know if I just use the `st.data_editor` object and corresponding `on_change` callback in a way that they were not meant to be used (passing/using the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` in the callback).
-> Is there another method to handle user edits on a dataframe, which ensures that those edits are processed exactly once, so neither multiple times nor never before the Streamlit page or `st.fragment` get reloaded?

### Why?

This is relevant when streaming user edits to a backend database, as potentially user edits are send multiple times to the backend, which causes unnecessary traffic, or edits are lost and not sent to the backend at all.

### How?

Solution (including filtering of the `st.data_editor`'s session state and locking threads during the `on_change` callback):
```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import threading
import time

st.set_page_config(layout="wide")

# Initialize session state variables if not already done
if "applied_edits" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["applied_edits"] = {}
if "df" not in st.session_state:
    data = np.zeros((1000, 30))
    columns = [f"Column {i + 1}" for i in range(30)]
    df_init = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=columns)
    totals_row = pd.DataFrame(df_init.sum(axis=0)).T
    st.session_state.df = pd.concat([totals_row, df_init], ignore_index=True)
    st.session_state.df["Totals"] = st.session_state.df.sum(axis=1)
if "call" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["call"] = 0
if "lock" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["lock"] = threading.Lock()


def df_on_change(df):
    with st.session_state["lock"]:
        print(f"on_change call: {st.session_state['call']}")
        # Get a copy of all edited rows in this session
        all_edits = st.session_state["df_editor"]["edited_rows"]
        # Filter out the new edits/changes that were/are not processed in a previous call of the df_on_change function
        edited_rows = {
            row: {
                col: val
                for col, val in changes.items()
                if (row not in st.session_state["applied_edits"])
                or (st.session_state["applied_edits"][row].get(col) != val)
            }
            for row, changes in all_edits.items()
        }
        # Update the record of applied edits so the filter above can be applied in the next call of the df_on_change function once again
        for row, changes in edited_rows.items():
            if not changes:
                continue  # no new changes for this row
            if row not in st.session_state["applied_edits"]:
                st.session_state["applied_edits"][row] = {}
            for col, val in changes.items():
                st.session_state["applied_edits"][row][col] = val

        # Log the filtered edits for debugging
        print(f"session state of data editor: {st.session_state['df_editor']}")
        print(f"New edits to apply: {edited_rows}")
        print(f"Applied edits history: {st.session_state['applied_edits']}")

        # Apply the new changes to the DataFrame
        for row, changes in edited_rows.items():
            for col, val in changes.items():
                print(f"writing value {val} to row {row} and column {col}")
                df.loc[row, col] = val
                # simulate a on_change function that requires a long execution time
                time.sleep(1)

        # Recompute totals row based on all data below it
        df.loc[0] = df.iloc[1:].sum(axis=0)
        df["Totals"] = df.sum(axis=1)

        st.toast("Data updated successfully!")
        st.session_state["call"] += 1


# Use st.data_editor with the on_change callback
st.data_editor(
    st.session_state.df,
    use_container_width=True,
    num_rows="fixed",
    disabled=["Totals"],  # prevent editing the totals row
    column_order=[f"Column {i + 1}" for i in range(30)] + ["Totals"],
    key="df_editor",
    on_change=df_on_change,
    args=[st.session_state.df],
    row_height=20,
)
```

In the demo videos below, the user first adds 9 cells at once and then does single cell changes afterwards (on other cells).

Demo video of the code above (terminal output also shows that each edit/cell is just processed once, which is not the case when not filtering the `st.data_editor`'s session state):

Within the last couple of weeks, the "Bad message format" popup started appearing in my commercial application that uses Streamlit for the UI. We have not deployed a new version, changed the Docker container, or changed the application hosting. The Bad message format was not a problem before.

title: Rerun() inside an st.fragment resets widget values to defaults.
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `rerun()` is called inside a fragment, it resets assigned values and session_state of contained input widgets to defaults.

E.g., for the attached code, when you click the "rerun" button, both _displayed_ values of `t` change to "foo", regardless of what was entered in the text box. Also, if no default is provided for the input, it resets to an empty string.

Note that if `rerun()` is called _after_ the input widget, everything works as expected.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment()
def toggle_and_text():
    if st.button("rerun"):
        st.rerun()
    t = st.text_input("Enter t:",value='foo', key='t')
    st.info(f't = {t}')

toggle_and_text()
st.header('Outside Fragment')
st.info(f'session_state_t = {st.session_state.t}')
st.button("Update")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the example code
2. Change the text input value
3. Click "rerun"
4. The value displayed changes back to "foo"

### Expected Behavior

The widget input state should not change when doing a rerun()

### Current Behavior

Widget input assigned values and state are reset to defaults when doing a rerun() inside a fragment, _unless rerun() appears after the widget_.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.45.0
- Python version: 3.13.2
- Operating System: MasOS 15.1
- Browser: Safari, Chrome, and Brave


### Additional Information

_No response_

title: Disable st.data_editor by cell (and row): cell/row-level editability
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

**Current Behavior**: Only full columns of an `st.data_editor` can be enabled or disabled for user-editing.

**Feature Request**: Allow for assigning editability on cell (and row) level. For example, an editable column should be disabled for cells (rows) where a certain condition is met.

**Workaround**: Currently, there is no functional workaround. I tried to implement a customized handling of the user input to catch undesired edits and raise an exception when a user edits a cell that should not be editable (in a non-disabled column). However the session_state (e.g. `st.session_state[<data_editor_key>]["edited_rows"].items()`)of the `st.data_editor` does not allow for manipulating the user-input, so the user has to manually undo their changes or refresh the streamlit page and (potentially) re-enter all other edits (in case of bulk edits).


### Why?

- Cell or row-level editability is crucial in scenarios where there are dependent or virtual rows, such as sub-totals. 
- Additionally, there may be other differences between rows or columns that necessitate cell-level assigned editability. For example, allowing more columns to be edited for rows that are newly added by the user via the `st.data_editor`.

### How?

1. Change the `disabled`parameter to a `cell_disabled` parameter: A dictionary where keys are column names and values are lists of row indices or conditions that specify which cells should be disabled.
2. Intermediate solution (set editability on row level for non-disabled columns or all columns): Keep the `disabled` parameter as a `column_disabled` parameter and add an additional parameter `row_disabled`: A list of row indices or conditions that specify which entire rows should be disabled.

### Additional Context

title: Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Today, when a page is refreshed / app gets rerun / data for dataframe changes, the dataframe completely refreshes. Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position are lost. 

This makes it hard to work with data within the dataframe and change it by means of a Master Detail View for example.

Idea is: Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe when data is reloaded / the page is rerun.


### Why?

Scenario: A Master Detail View: The dataframe is part of the Master View within the page, and the Detail View enables the user to edit certain fields (not all are visible in the dataframe). After changing some data, the dataframe is reloaded and selection, sorting, scrolling position are lost.

### How?

The selection currently is set in the session, but it is not considered when the page is reloaded. 

Sorting is not part of the state.

Scrolling position is preserved for st.container today, but not for st.dataframe.

Solution idea:
- Store selection and sorting in session_state and use this information when the page is rerun and the dataframe is rendered.
- Use the implementation of st.container to preserve scrolling position.

### Additional Context


This issue is related to, however they only cover parts of this idea. 

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8851
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10128

title: Fragment to fragment (co-fragment) communication instead of rerunning entire app
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Would be great to create a functionality for co-fragment communication directly rather than re-running the entire app. This could be streamlit's blockhain moment - no middle men (in this case the entire app).

### Why?

Re-rendering the entire app for co-fragment communication is frustration slow. Co-fragment communication would drastically increase the speed and performance of a streamlit app. 

### How?

My app looks like the below:

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

The black outlines are fragments. The purple/pink outlines are nested fragments. I understand co-fragment communication occurs through session_state which is great but for this communication to be recognised, one must re-run the whole app. This makes the app more slow and somewhat buggy in my experience of operating my app. 

Seeing as fragments can be re-run periodically, it would be great to add the possibility to communicate between specific fragments via an action. For example, in my app image, After I input details in the "Contact Details" expander, I want to update the CV Preview fragment. But to do that, I have to re-run the entire app. Perhaps the possibility to rerun specific fragments based on some unique Id (like a key of a streamlit widget) when I say click on the submit form button in the Contact Details expander would be great. 

Just an example
```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"])
```

The issue with the above is for every rerun action, the `keys to update` will rerun. So perhaps, we could create a trigger command parameter.

```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=["form_submit_btn"])
```

We could also get fancy and connect trigger keys to keys to update:


```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=[{"frag1":"form_submit_btn"}])
```
