title: st.bind() to attach query_params to session state
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

J. Carroll (before he left his position on the team) and I were discussing possible implementations of a new way to integrate `st.query_params` and `st.session_state` on Discord back in March. I am writing this proposal to officially document the idea and see if there's anyone on the Streamlit team who would be willing to "greenlight" this feature or give me a sense of whether it would be welcome.

At it's core, `st.bind()` is a way to declare certain elements of `st.session_state` (including widget values) permanently bound to a corresponding value in `st.query_params` (and by extension, the browser's URL). A basic example of `st.bind()` looks like this:

```python
import streamlit as st

st.bind("user_text")

user_text = st.text_input("Show me what you got", key="user_text", value="rhythm")

st.write("You got", user_text)
```

If you navigate to this page at http://localhost:8501/, you will see 
```
Show me what you got: [  rhythm      ]
You got rhythm
```
and the URL will be updated to http://localhost:8501/?user_text=rhythm

If you navigate to this page at http://localhost:8501/?user_text=music, you will see 
```
Show me what you got: [  music      ]
You got music
```

Any changes to the value of the `text_input` widget are immediately reflected in the page URL.

### Why?

This makes it extremely easy to create "stateful" apps that can be shared with people. Have a dashboard that shows you popularity of different music genres by country and year? With `st.bind()` you can reflect the user inputs for `year` and `genre` into the URL, and then send that URL to someone else so they can pull up the dashboard in the exact same state:

* https://popmusicmap.streamlit.app/?year=2010&genre=funk
* https://popmusicmap.streamlit.app/?year=2012&genre=R%26B&genre=country&genre=gospel

```python
import streamlit as st
from my_app import music_popularity_map, genre_options

st.bind(["year", "genre"])

year = st.number_input("Pick a year", key="year", min_value=2000, max_value=2023)
genres = st.multiselect("Pick some genres", key="genre" options=genre_options)

music_popularity_map(year, genres)
```

What does this feature offer over just using `st.query_params`? It avoids a lot of boilerplate and conversion code, for one. To do this without `st.bind` would require a lot of legwork:

```python
import streamlit as st
from my_app import music_popularity_map, genre_options

year_string_from_url = st.query_params.get("year", "2000")
try:
     st.session_state.year = int(year_string_from_url)
except ValueError:
     pass

def update_year_callback():
    if "year" in st.session_state:
        st.query_params.year = str(st.session_state.year)

year = st.number_input("Pick a year", key="year", min_value=2000, max_value=2023, on_change=update_year_callback)
genres = st.multiselect("Pick some genres", key="genre" options=genre_options)

music_popularity_map(year, genres)
````
And all that for just ONE widget!

My own extension's demo, https://query-string.streamlit.app/, has some other examples of the kinds of things you can do with this kind of feature. Due to not having access to all of the streamlit session state internals, it is limited to a smaller selection of widgets and tends to be a bit finicky with some of the more complex widgets like `datetime` or `slider`.

I think an officially supported version of this would benefit a lot of people who are building apps with streamlit.

### How?

`st.bind()` can be implemented as an exposed method of `SafeSessionStateProxy -> SafeSessionState -> SessionState`, which already has access to both `query_params` and `session_state`.

Calling `st.bind("foo")` places a new `BindRegistration` into a datastructure within `SessionState`:
```python
_bind_registry = {
   "foo": BindRegistration("foo", serde=None, deserde=None, plural=None),
   ...
}
```
Values are deserialized into `st.session_state` lazily, meaning a call to `st.session_state.get(key)` will check to see if there is a `BindRegistration` for `key` and will deserialize and return the value without it ever needing to go into any of the existing `SessionState` storage dictionaries.

Because all query params are strings, widgets will supply additional "hints" when calling `register_widget` about what type of object they would like to receive back. If the user did not call `st.bind("foo")` with any additional arguments, then a `st.text_input(key="foo")` will receive `st.query_params.foo` as a string when it registers itself, while a `st.number_input(key="foo", value=0)` would suggest that it wants an integer, and `register_widget` would attempt to deserialize `st.query_params.foo` to an integer.

When a script re-run is triggered, any keyed widgets whose value changed and whose key has a corresponding `BindRegistration` are re-serialized and pushed to the frontend to be updated in the browsers URL bar. This behavior will be made even more seamless once https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/9049 is incorporated, as the app will be able to send these new parameters along with other `NewSession` data at the start of the Rerun, instead of having to rely on a separate `PageInfoChanged` message.

Users could also have the capability to express their own serialization and deserialization methods for each `st.bind()` call, allowing for advanced extensibility of the behavior. 


### Additional Context

If anyone is willing to play coordinator on this feature, I'm more than happy to work on it with the Streamlit team on whatever timeline they feel is appropriate.

title: Non-Blocking Async Progress Bar
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

An async progress bar that allows one to continue to navigate existing data while progress is made on background analysis and/or artifact generation.

### Why?

I am working on a project where I have items in a dataframe and I can see existing artifacts regarding that data. When a add more data to the dataframe, I want to generate new artifacts associated to the new data, and possibly update the artifacts of the existing data as needed. But I don't want that background processing to hinder the review of data that is currently available and I want to review any new artifacts as they become available via the background process. And I want a progress bar that tells me how many item have been processed so far. Unfortunately, there is no way I have seen to get around the fact that st.progress blocks the main interaction and update thread.

### How?

#### Function Signatures

   - async_progress(ss_name='async_prog_bar', async_func=async_func, af_args=[af_args], af_kwargs={af_kwargs})
       - The async_progress object upon instantiation should check for existing state in the session_state object and update itself accordingly.
       - Then it should spawn an async thread within the __main__ block that periodically updates the progress bar data in the session_state object.
       - The async thread should stop if it can no-longer find it's associated data in the session_state object.
       - The async thread should also enable a url (http://localhost:9504/async/<session_id>/<element_name>) to receive update requests from an async java script that is associated to the progress bar element on the web page, which it periodically updates.
   - async_func(ss_prog_bar: str, *args, **kwargs) 
       - async_func must be async ie. 'async def async_func()'
       - async_func modifies the progress bar by referencing and updating the ss_prog_bar element the session_state object.
       - if async_func is itself generates threads, then only the main thread should update the progress bar.
       - async_func should stop if it can no-longer find it's associated progress-bar data in the session_state object.

#### async_progress annotations

   - @st.async_progress
      - Indicates that the function is an async_progress function.
      - Validates and/or sets the function to be async.

import streamlit as st

@st.experimental_fragment()
def foo(offset: int, foo_counter: int):
    with st.container(border=True):
        st.write(f"{offset = }; {foo_counter = }")
        full_counter = offset + foo_counter
        toggle_key = f"toggle_{full_counter}"
        toggle_value = f"{toggle_key}_value"    
        st.session_state[toggle_value] = st.toggle(
            label=f"Foo {full_counter}",
            value=st.session_state.get(toggle_value, False),
            key=toggle_key,
        )
        st.write(f"session_state.{toggle_value} = {st.session_state[toggle_value]}")


def main():
    st.write(f"Running Streamlit {st.__version__}")
    colA, _= st.columns((1, 1))
    with colA:
        offset = st.number_input(
            label="Offset", min_value=0, max_value=50, value=0, step=10

    for x in range(1, 4):

if __name__ == "__main__":

title: Disable rerun on user resize window or interact with application (froze interface) when heavy tasks are running, with global thread state
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I'm just wondering if is possible to **disable** reruning on user resize window or interact with application (froze interface) when heavy tasks are running, with global thread state or similar.

Because, I already see all documentation, blogs and issues related, but solutions are not fitted to our problem.

### Why?

# Context
We have a Front (streamlit) with connection with other micro-services (FastAPIs), and I know we can change to an event service approach, but is more suitable for us in this moment, to have an option in streamlit to not reruning the application if it isrunning specific tasks in the script thread.

# Problem
So when my application (Streamlit) sends a request streaming the response of a micro-service, if I a user cliks or resizes, or interacts with other component in the interface, streamlit it raises a StopException, because has to rerun, but my streaming response is still running and updating the interface, we don't want to rerun or take care of user interaction until specific process ends.

### How?

# Feature Propose
We noted that this behaviour is more notorious in the last update in streamlit~=1.36.0. So we just wondering, if there is a way or can be a way to encapsulates some runing process, and do not stops until it ends. In addition, we want to use all streamlit stuff inside that process, because want to update the interface or session_state, while we recieve the streaming response.

A functional approach can be to have a global lock, that all the code inside this block, cannot be stoppable until it ends, so interactions when enter on this blocks are blocked or enqueued, or give to the developer the control to manage this rerun.

I know that blocks of freeze interaction is not user friendly, but sometimes it needed, maybe showing in the interface a loader dialog or something similar, to make understand to the user that this cannot be cancelable or similar

title: st.selectbox could be typed so that it always returns T unless the index is None (etc)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, the return type of [selectbox](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/1b73b444fe118b65f20957166f216b0e83a23e00/lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/selectbox.py#L79) is `T | None`. As far as I know, the only way for selectbox to return `None` is if `index` is `None` or if `OptionSequence[T]` is empty (`OptionSequence[]`?). These conditions could be added to the type signature of selectbox using [overloads](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/more_types.html#function-overloading), and then in my program I wouldn't have to `assert` or `str` the results of every st.selectbox. There would be one or two overloads that returned `None | T` and one that returned just `T`. NoReturn could also possibly be added to the return type union, because if you choose an invalid index the function will error and never return.

Or maybe this goal is doomed. My project uses a lot of https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state#session-state-and-widget-state-association stuff like:

```python
import streamlit as st
st.session_state.name = "Max"
st.selectbox("Your name", ["Sam", "Max"], key="name")
```

and I don't really know how to account for this in static typing, because the program could set the session_state value of the widget to `None`.

Furthermore, it may be unavoidable that there's always the possibility of an error in rendering, or suchlike, that would cause the widget to return None. I don't know enough to say.

So, I think this typing feature is desirable, but it may be impossible.


### Why?

Currently, whenever I use a selectbox in my typed project, I have to deal with the type union somehow each time, even though the result should always be of a certain type, which is a bit annoying.

title: Move st.app_state further up in the roadmap
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

State management has been by far the most common complaint about Streamlit online when I was comparing various dashboarding libraries. There is a mention of `st.app_state` in the roadmap, which is great, but there is no timeline of when it will go into development / be finished. I would like to suggest that this `st.app_state` be given a definite date, ideally as soon as possible. 

I also saw that NoSQL database mentioned, I would suggest considering pickling the entire `st.session_state`. It'll be faster and more robust in almost every way -- there is no network trip to the database, no need to occupy an extra process running the database, no lookups, and minimal serialization. It also works for any data type, and as far as speed goes for large binaries, what you wouldn't pickle you wouldn't store in a NoSQL database anyway. 

I would further propose that as opposed to having to register data in `st.session_state`, have all state data be registered by default. This comes from personal experience where my code is bloated by 50-100% from having to save and load every single thing into `session_state`, and it's usually the exception that I have a truly stateless component. 

### Why?

Given how many people the app reruns issue impacts, and literally everyone handling their own way, it would seem logical to make this a priority. From looking at the up-coming todos, I think st.app_state has the highest impact, as measured by
```
no. of hours saved * no. of streamlit users affected / development hour
```

For example, I have a custom component dedicated to state management, which saves and loads yaml, among other things,  and I'm almost certain that I'm not the only one. And as mentioned, almost 50% of my code is related to checking, saving to, or loading from `st.session_data`, and I've spent more time than I want on thinking about caching.

### How?

I'm open to however it's planned to be developed, but it seems wrong to me that an app would rerun the script from top to bottom on every interaction as a foundation. But, I'm unfamiliar with how streamlit works under the hood, so what I say could be misguided. 

Having developed in Angular and React, my two cents is to adopt some kind of model-view-controller (MVC) framework in the background. Generally events / interactions should only propagate up to the component it affects, and no further. My understanding is that these components are usually modelled as trees. 

How this can be done without changing the API is more difficult, and above my pay-grade. 

### Additional Context

To me `st.session_state` and various caching mechanisms are bandaid solutions that puts off dealing with the much larger issue related to the app rerunning from top to bottom on every interaction. In other words, if streamlit was stateful by default, there wouldn't be a need for session states and far fewer occasions where caching is needed. I'm not sure the proposed `st.app_state` is intended to address that underlying issue of the app rerunning on each interaction, as at face value it sounds like what will hopefully be the last fix -- which is ok if that's the best we can get.

title: New component: `st.drawer` as a dismissable container
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit has expanded its layout options, which compound on each others to create complex application user flows beyond the single page, top to bottom interaction. 

As `st.dialog` is coming along, and `st.popover` merged, most types of surfaces are being covered by streamlit, except the drawer concept, which is a dismissable container sliding from the right of the screen on demand, which blocks the screen from the side without masking the context, can be used as an information surface, for continuous interactions (like LLM Chat), or for form input. 

### Why?

`st.sidebar`, which is the current closest equivalent has been very useful to have a permanent set of widget independent of the main window context but fall short when

- The interface has to be conditional, it requires more `session_state `trickery to redraw the sidebar
- The navigation gets rich, and the sidebar should have only a few other static elements but not a full form entry / sub interface

Thus, the sidebar and drawer concepts may overlap for simple usage, but are very different in practice and we would beneficiate from a better separation of duty 

Gitlab makes a good example of using a rich navigation sidebar to the left hand side, and drawers for Gitlab Duo AI Chat, or to input CI Variables

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### How?

The [Base Web](https://baseweb.design/components/drawer/) component is a starting point.

The main behaviours between the background and drawer I can refine in a first round are : 

- _Focused_ : The background is frozen, the user must exit using a default exit button. Clicking on the background does not exit the drawer (as it leads to different input errors). A drawer is always exitable. The background gets slightly greyed out, to ensure the drawer is in focus but remains readable
- _Scrollable_ : The background can be scrolled. This ensures that the user can retain a mental image of where they are in the UX Flow of the app.
- _Form Like (Optional)_ : The developer should be able to set a condition which closes the drawer, similar to how `st.form_submit_button` allows to exit the form. Perhaps we could reuse behaviours, and a form could be nested within a drawer, upon submission it closes the drawer.

With only those basic behaviour we can address most use cases:

1. A one-shot configuration (i.e. use a drawer to make a request, drawer closes and request shows up in main app area)
2. A continuous data entry, where the drawer remains open whilst the user makes several input (i.e. add multiple records)
3. An information/documentation panel with little interactions, but potentially rich display elements
4. A chat like interface on demand, a la copilot or gitlab duo chat.

On the python end, `st.drawer` should be similar syntaxically to st.dialog and st.popover to ease on the cognitive load, meaning

```python
with st.drawer("Open Drawer"):
   ...

```

Should call the drawer to expand, clicking away or on a well visible close/exit button should close the drawer.

### Additional Context

### Additional Context

Similar issues arise because components have no callbacks.

body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I would like to work on adding a new container variation to Streamlit called `st.skeleton`. The `SkeletonElement` proto was added by [USER] in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/7598 as a way to allow the Streamlit Scriptrunner to display a small loading animation while it was still waiting to start rendering elements to the page. However, at the time, no means was added to allow Streamlit app developers to use the new Skeleton element themselves.

This proposal outlines how _I_ think the new `st.skeleton` feature should function. It is also a call for discussion -- if you think this feature goes too far or not far enough, please let me know. If you would personally find a feature like this useful, please upvote.

### Why?

I think the Skeleton element has significant value as a way to allow app developers to separate -- both structurally and temporally -- the definition of their app's UI from the sometimes-IO-constrained process of fetching and rendering data. **an `st.skeleton` as defined in this proposal thus represents the promise of content to the end application user**

### How?

`st.skeleton` is fundamentally just an `st.empty` with a future promise of additional content (typically just one chart or plot or table or "thing" per skeleton)

### Call Signature
```python
st.skeleton(width=0.5, height=100, callback=my_function, autocallback=False)
# Width and height of the skeleton are configurable. Fractional values for width are treated as a percentage, 
# while values >1 are treated as a minimum pixel size.
```

### What does it look like?
See https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/7598
- May decide to add a third keywrod option to choose between an `AppSkeleton` and a `Skeleton` style animation but for now 

### What's the basic use case?
It's most basic use is a drop-in replacement for `st.empty()`. 
Like an empty, `st.skeleton()` returns a special SkeletonDeltaGenerator context manager object.
When you call another DeltaGenerator mixin function on it, it behaves just like an empty, and the skeleton animation that was playing is replaced by the new content. So this
```python
# Draw UI
st.write("Census Data")
census_data_placeholder = st.empty()  # The empty is a collapsed element
year = st.selectbox("Select Year", options=[2022, 2023, 2024])

# Get data from source
# assume function call takes a long time
census_dataframe = get_census_data_from_database(year)

# Draw the data, causing it to "pop" in above the year selectbox.
census_data_placeholder.dataframe(census_dataframe)
```
becomes
```python
# Draw UI
st.write("Census Data")
census_data_placeholder = st.skeleton(height=500px)  # The skeleton holds space for the future data
year = st.selectbox("Select Year", options=[2022, 2023, 2024])

# Get data from source, assume this takes a long time
census_dataframe = get_census_data_from_database(year)

# Draw the data, replacing the skeleton animation that was previously there
census_data_placeholder.dataframe(census_dataframe)
```

In this case (and as you will see below, in this case only) replacement can happen multiple times:
```python
skeleton = st.skeleton()

# User is shown a skeleton animation while data1 loads
data1 = get_data_long_running_function()
skeleton.dataframe(data1)

# User sees data1 while data2 loads, then data1 is replaced
data2 = get_data_another_long_running_function()
skeleton.dataframe(data2)
```

### Use as a context manager
When you use `st.skeleton()` in a `with` statement, it first places an `st.container` inside of itself
and then sets that as the DeltaGenerator context, allowing you to write natural code like:
```python
# Draw UI
st.write("Census Data")
census_data_placeholder = st.skeleton(height=500px)
year = st.selectbox("Select Year", options=[2022, 2023, 2024])

# Get data from source, assume this takes a long time
census_dataframe = get_census_data_from_database(year)
census_statistics = compute_statistics(census_dataframe)

# Draw the data, replacing the skeleton animation that was previously there
# Both the st.dataframe and the st.write are dispalyed inside of an st.container
# inside of the skeleton
with census_data_placeholder:
    st.dataframe(census_dataframe)
    st.write(census_statistics)
```

If only implemented up to this point in the proposal `st.skeleton` is still useful as a way to have an `st.empty` take up space in a page's UI. This avoids "pop-in" data that changes the layout of the UI significantly for the end user -- which is a problem that can currently happen with `st.empty`

### Getting fancy with callbacks
Going beyond basic `st.empty` functionality, `st.skeleton` also has a `callback` argument which allows you to queue up some function to be run at a later time. The callback function is assumed to itself call into one or more Streamlit elements. It can be run directly by calling `.load(*args, **kwargs)` on the `SkeletonDeltaGenerator`. The callback function acts as if it were being run inside a `with skeleton:` block, e.g.
```python
skeleton = st.skeleton(callback=my_function)
# ... more code
skeleton.load(a, b, c)
```
is equivalent to
```python
skeleton = st.skeleton()
# ... more code
with skeleton:
   my_function(a, b, c)
```

As an example:
```python
def render_census_data(year):
    # Get data from source, assume this takes a long time
    census_dataframe = get_census_data_from_database(year)
    census_statistics = compute_statistics(census_dataframe)
    # Draw the data
    st.dataframe(census_dataframe)
    st.write(census_statistics)

# Draw UI
st.write("Census Data")
census_data_placeholder = st.skeleton(height=500px, callback=render_census_data)
year = st.selectbox("Select Year", options=[2022, 2023, 2024])

# Load the census data and display it in place of the skeleton by running
# the callback function.
census_data_placeholder.load(year)
```

### Lions and Tigers and Autocallbacks, Oh my!
Where callbacks can _really_ shine is via an "autocallback" feature. This is a user-configurable feature which is enabled
by default. When an `st.skeleton()` call with a callback function is encountered, it will register itself with the current `ScriptRunner`. At the end of a successful and complete page execution, the ScriptRunner will then call `.load()` on all of the `SkeletonDeltaGenerator`s that meet the following criteria:
1. the `.load()` method was not already called on them by the user
2. they have a valid element path on the front end (meaning they haven't been _replaced_ by any other content yet)

`.load()` is called in the order that the `st.skeleton()` was first encountered. There may be additional limitations (such as enforcing that callback functions do not modify session_state or something like that.

When autocallback is enabled (by default), the st.skeleton() also accepts `args` and `kwargs` parameters since
there will be no calling of the `load` function.
```python
# Draw UI
st.write("Census Data")
year = st.selectbox("Select Year", options=[2022, 2023, 2024])
census_data_placeholder = st.skeleton(height=500px, callback=render_census_data, args=[year])

# The callback render_census_data is automatically called at the end of script execution with the argument `year`
```
Optional: the SkeletonDeltaGenerator also has a `.set_callback_arguments(*args, **kwargs)` method so that parameters
can be set even after the SkeletonDeltaGenerator is created
```python
# Draw UI
st.write("Census Data")
census_data_placeholder = st.skeleton(height=500px, callback=render_census_data)
year = st.selectbox("Select Year", options=[2022, 2023, 2024])
census_data_placeholder.set_callback_args(year)
```
And you can turn it off via a global config option or a keyword argument
```python
census_data_placeholder = st.skeleton(height=500px, callback=render_census_data, autocallback=False)
```

title: session_state stats are not tracked correctly on metrics endpoint
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit provides a metrics endpoint that exposes information about memory usage by cache and session_state at `/_stcore/metrics`. Based on the inspection of the contents and the response type header, this is intended to follow the [OpenMetrics standard](https://github.com/OpenObservability/OpenMetrics/blob/main/specification/OpenMetrics.md).

However for the session_state metric, I obseved that when multiple sessions are active the endpoint prints multiple lines, one for each session, with the same labels. E.g.

```sh
% curl localhost:8501/_stcore/metrics
# TYPE cache_memory_bytes gauge
# UNIT cache_memory_bytes bytes
# HELP Total memory consumed by a cache.
cache_memory_bytes{cache_type="st_session_state",cache=""} 4848
cache_memory_bytes{cache_type="st_session_state",cache=""} 4248
cache_memory_bytes{cache_type="st_session_state",cache=""} 4248
```

This breaks the OpenMetric standard which states that a metric name + set of label values must be unique and appear only once in a response.

### Reproducible Code Example

_No response_

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run any streamlit app
2. Open multiple sessions, such as by navigating to the app on two tabs
3. Call `curl localhost:8501/_stcore/metrics` (or whatever the host/port is)
4. Observe multiple session state lines with identical labels

### Expected Behavior

Each line in the result will be unique.

### Current Behavior

Multiple lines with the same name and labels.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.29
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: MacOS
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

I believe the [function that needs to be fixed is here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/1.29.0/lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py#L671-L676)

Suggested fix would be to either:
* Sum the memory usage of all sessions and record it in one line, OR
* Add a session_id label to each line so they labels are distinct

For a quick fix, I would suggest the first option.

But since it is closed (due to the user not really needing the particular use case) I have opened this new one with another simple minimum reproducible example.

### Reproducible Code Example

[[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7749)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# using session state, works ever other input:
if "df" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.df = pd.DataFrame({"In":[0,1,2],"Out":[0,0,0]})
st.session_state.df = st.data_editor(st.session_state.df)
st.session_state.df["Out"] = st.session_state.df["In"]**2
st.write(st.session_state.df)

# # works every input but the df is not updated in data_editor:
# df = pd.DataFrame({"In":[0,1,2],"Out":[0,0,0]})
# df = st.data_editor(df)
# df["Out"] = df["In"]**2
# st.write(df)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click on a field in the in column.
2. Input a number, enter.
3. Watch for changes in the dataframes.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that each input in the data_editor to result in the rest of the code to run, before it loops back to the top and into the data_editor with new data which is displayed.
In this example I expect the "state" version to behave just like the "non-state" example, with the added functionality of the state of course.

### Current Behavior

1. I input a number(say 5) in a input field press enter.
2. This new input is replaced with the previous value instantly.
3. I input 5 in the same box again.
4. The edit_data frame now has the correct input, but not the updated input. The st.write frame is updated to reflect the correct values.

Another variant:
1. I input 5 in row 1. -> instantly replaced, nothing in st.write
2. I input 4 in row 2. -> editor: input is updated, output is not. st.write: row two is updated.
3. I input 3 in row 3. -> editor: row 2 is updated, row 3 ignored. Both editor and write now agrees.
OR: in another box I input a changed number (not the same as exists already, that doesnt do anything)

Pretty hard to explain, please try for yourself to get an idea how it really behaves.
Basically the state of data_editor is always one loop behind in updating, and the input seems to dissapear until another change is made.

### Is this a regression?

title: Coming soon: API update for Streamlit query params
body:
Hi all, an FYI that we’re [working on](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/7664) an upgrade to Streamlit’s [query params API](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/utilities/st.experimental_get_query_params). I’m sharing about it today to get feedback on the new API and help assess whether to release it as `experimental_` or go directly to a stable API. Take a look and let us know what you think!

### Current state

Query params support is a fairly popular feature for providing some state or input about an app as part of the URL, making it easier to share with users or collaborators in a given state. Today it’s supported in Streamlit with two methods, [experimental_get_query_params](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/utilities/st.experimental_get_query_params) and [experimental_set_query_params](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/utilities/st.experimental_set_query_params).

Both methods treat the query params as a single blob and require the app developer to track and manage the state (in case of multiple params) and handle list conversion.

```python
st.experimental_set_query_params(
    show_map=True,
    selected=["asia", "america"],
)
# Output URL: localhost:8501/?show_map=True&selected=asia&selected=america

# Now return value if I call get
st.experimental_get_query_params()
{"show_map": ["True"], "selected": ["asia", "america"]}
```

### Planned API update

Our plan is to move query params to a dict-like API similar to `st.session_state`, where Streamlit tracks the state of all query params and app developers can interact with them independently. For query params with only a single value, this also means the developer doesn’t need to worry about list conversion.

```python
st.query_params["show_map"] = True
st.query_params["selected"] = ["asia", "america"]
# Same output URL as above

# Note we convert everything to str return type
st.query_params["show_map"] # returns "True"
st.query_params.show_map # also works, returns "True"
```

### Handling lists and multiple values

A key concern for query parameters is handling multiple values. For normal get / retrieval calls on `query_params`, Streamlit will return **only the last value set for the given key**, whether in the URL directly via Streamlit API. To retrieve a list of all set values, developers can call `st.query_params.get_all(key)`. This approach is typical of several other python web API frameworks such as [tornado](https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/stable/web.html#tornado.web.RequestHandler.get_query_argument) and [flask](https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/blob/2.3.6/src/werkzeug/datastructures/structures.py#L118-L128). 

```python
# URL: localhost:8501/?show_map=True&selected=asia&selected=america

st.query_params["selected"]
# "america"

st.query_params.get_all("selected")
# ["asia", "america"]

st.query_params.get_all("show_map")
# ["True"]
```

### Other improvements

We’ll also be making a few quality improvements to the existing support and making sure less common cases like setting an empty string / blank value are supported.

### What do you think?

Let us know your feedback about the changes. Our current plan is to release this minimal version, which simplifies the API for typical use cases and leaves room to extend to new features in the future such as better handling for type conversion, or binding query params to certain session_state keys or widget values.

Your input can help impact whether we release this immediately as `st.query_params` or do an `st.experimental_query_params` to see more usage of the new API before finalizing it.

Thank you!

title: Streamlit Crashing with Error: `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

**UPDATE**: I believe the culprit is a bug in the `@st.cache_resource` logic and/or the way streamlit handles db connections that try to persist (had same issues using `session_state`). See my follow-up message below. 

My initial issue:

Unfortunately I have a fairly complicated app. My streamlit application is crashing and I'm not sure why. The error seems somewhat ominous, but there's really not much information that helps me figure out what's going on, which is why I've made this issue. 

I've seen this error on rare occasion when building my complex application. Normally, this happens after I update the file and hit 'rerun', so I just chalk it up to: something happens when I hot-reload a new version of the file that breaks things. Nothing I'm concerned about since I don't expect to do this in production.

However, after adding a normal [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/widgets/st.selectbox), streamlit intermittently crashes when I use [this](https://github.com/hoggatt/st-combobox) simple custom component that gives me the ability to define my own auto complete function. I don't actually think it's related to the combobox itself, it's just that when the combobox is auto-completing, it's rerunning a lot. This was working before I added a normal `st.textbox`, but now it's completely broken. However, the fact that I saw it very infrequently before indicates to me it's probably not directly related to the selectbox. 


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# THIS IS PSEUDO-CODE #

search_input = st.text_input()

...
many conditional statements doing something with the search input including setting st.experimental_set_query_params at one point
also queries the database using a cached_resource mysql connector (see below)
...

value = st.selectbox(items based on search_input)

# allow selecting something using a combobox (st-combobox) with autocomplete
def search_files(searchterm):
  refine search based (in part) on value
selected_value = st_combobox(search_files, ...)

# this method is cached
file = get_file(selected_value)

...
setting up controls for the plot based on the file loaded
uses st.experimental_set_query_params at some point
no database or complex cached stuff
...

# make plotly plot(s) here
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Unfortunately I'm not able to figure out exactly why this happens. It doesn't seem to happen consistently. 

However, often I see this error nearby: `2013 (HY000): Lost connection to MySQL server during query`. 

I have a method that looks like this:
```
@st.cache_resource
def loaddb():
    creds = ...
    dbconn = SQL("EXAMPLE", "example.com", creds["username"], creds["password"], True)
    return dbconn
```

### Expected Behavior

I expect this crash not to happen. 

### Current Behavior

This is all that happens. Streamlit prints out two lines in the console, then hard-crashes:
```
free(): double free detected in tcache 2
Aborted
```

Sometimes I see this error too (maybe it's related to the cache_resource having issues?):
```
2013 (HY000): Lost connection to MySQL server during query
```
This error doesn't seem to crash outright, but something tells me it's related. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.26.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: Ubuntu 20.04
- Browser: Brave Version 1.57.62, Chromium: 116.0.5845.180 (Official Build) (64-bit)


### Additional Information

I'm going to be trying to nail down exactly why this issue is happening over the next few days (try to figure out how to reproduce it) but I wanted to make the issue now since it seems like a very strange error someone on the team might have insight into.

comments_data.body:
With some further digging, I've found out two very useful pieces of information:

1. If I type slowly into the combobox (so the app reloads less frequently), it does not crash nearly as often. 
2. If I remove the `@st.cache_resource` decorator from the `loaddb()` method described above, the app seems to work without any issues no matter how quickly/often it reloads (although the db connection is no longer cached). For those of you looking for a more satisfactory solution than "don't use cache", unfortunately the [st.session_state](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/session-state) api causes the same issues.

### My non-expert opinion

This `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` error is being generated in c++ or c code (possibly cpython stuff). My guess is that something in the `cache_resource` logic doesn't like very rapidly reloading the app (especially when the app has more complexity). My initial research indicates some variable is being freed in memory, then some other variable is being assigned to it. However, this only seems to happen in situations with more complex applications and frequent reloads. Since the `cache_resource` function is newer, my guess is there is some bug that shows up under these conditions with multiple threads/restarts. I hope this helps someone figure out what is going on.

I ran into the same error/behavior when trying to use `session_state` to store the database connection. This is strange and points to something a big deeper than just the cache_resource logic. Looks like restarting quickly in general + database connections that try to persist in any way cause issues.

I agree with your guess that it is coming from some C/C++ code, probably triggered by many reruns starting in separate threads at the same time and accessing the same database connection instance. Unfortunately this will be difficult to debug, and it isn't clear what we could do about it.
Closing this issue due to inactivity and it appears that it might not be directly related to Streamlit.

title: Built-In run_query with session_state
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

In conjunction with the st.experimental_connection feature, it would be nice to have sql queries that take one line of code. In addition, these queries could have an option to use existing results in a session_state if the query errors out

### Why?

These three components - the connection, the query and the error handling - all seem built out already and it would be nice to have them efficiently together as a built-in method

### How?

I'm not sure if the st.experimental_connection is included in the new method - it seems like that might be a separate first step and then step two would be something like st.run_query_with_handling(query: str, client: client, use_state: bool = True, state_name: str = None) to pull the data (client is a made-up type here, it would probably be a generic connection type defined in the class)

For st.run_query_with_handling, there could be two steps:

1. From https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/tutorials/databases/bigquery - as an example. Create a connection based on the conn_type and pull data with the query:

```
# Perform query.
# Uses st.cache_data to only rerun when the query changes or after 10 min.
@st.cache_data(ttl=600)
def run_query(query, client):
    query_job = client.query(query)
    rows_raw = query_job.result()
    # Convert to list of dicts. Required for st.cache_data to hash the return value.
    rows = [dict(row) for row in rows_raw]
    return rows
```

2. Create a wrapper that attempts the run #1 but uses existing results in st.session_state if use_state=True, else throws an error

```
def run_query_with_handling(query, client, use_state, state_name):
    try:
        output_data = query_func(query, client)
        st.session_state[state_name] = output_data
    except Exception as e:
        if state_name in st.session_state and use_state:
            log_str = (f"Unable to pull the most recent {state_name}, "
                       f"using data from the previous pull instead. "
                       f"Please check your internet connection and try "
                       f"again if necessary.\n"
                       f"Error: {e}")
            st.sidebar.warning(log_str)
            output_data = st.session_state[state_name]
        else:
            log_str = (f"*******************Error*******************\n"
                       f"Could not get {state_name}. If another error is "
                       f"not present, either {state_name} doesn't exist in "
                       f"the database or the connection is broken.\n"
                       f"Error: {e}")
            st.error(log_str)
    return output_data
```

Note that the output (st.sidebar.warning and st.error) seem like nice communication with the user, but could be optional or done in another way.

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: st.data_editor does not return added rows when dataframe from file
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.data_editor does not contain added rows when it is created out of a dataframe from a json loaded with st.file_uploader. The rows are visualized, but not accessible in the data_editor object.

- deleting rows works fine
- added rows are accessible in a roundabout way via st.session_state["key_of_data_editor"]

A forum post on this issue can be found here: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/adding-rows-in-st-data-editor-from-loaded-dataframe/46439

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]
[Saved_dataframe.txt](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/files/12031019/Saved_dataframe.txt)


### Reproducible Code Example

[[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6995)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd


def onchange():
    st.session_state.file_changed = True

# initialize Dataframe and state variables
if 'df' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.df = pd.DataFrame({'name': ["1", "2"], 'Type': None})
    st.session_state.file_changed = False
    st.session_state.loaded = False

# file upload
uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a file", on_change=onchange)
if uploaded_file is not None:
    st.session_state.loaded = True
    if st.session_state.file_changed == True:
        st.session_state.df = pd.read_json(uploaded_file)
        st.session_state.file_changed = False

# create editable Dataframe
edited_df = st.data_editor(
    st.session_state.df,
    num_rows="dynamic",
    hide_index=True,  # this is relevant for the workaround, not sure about the bug
    key='demo_df'
)

# bug: edited_df only contains the entire visualized content including added rows, if it was not loaded from file
# deleted rows are treated correctly though
st.write("edited_df:")
st.write(edited_df)
# path to workaround: the changes (from the loaded file) are visible in the df in session_state when accessed by key
st.write(st.session_state["demo_df"])
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. add row to data_editor --> OK: output dataframe shows added row
2. load example json file (attached or create a file with this content: `{"name": {"0": "0", "1": "1", "2": "2", "3": "3"}, "Type": {"0": null, "1": null, "2": null, "3": null}}`)
3. add row to data editor --> bug: output dataframe does not show added row

a workaround to get the visualized data:
`if st.session_state.loaded:
    fixed_df = pd.concat([edited_df, pd.DataFrame(st.session_state["demo_df"].get("added_rows"))])
else:
    fixed_df = edited_df
st.write(fixed_df)`

### Expected Behavior

data_editor should behave the same no matter where the dataframe used to create it comes from.

### Current Behavior

edited_df does not contain rows added in the GUI when it was created from a dataframe loaded via st.file_uploader

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Browser: Opera, Chrome

title: AppTest: synchronize query parameters when interacting with query-bound widgets
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Please make AppTest's widget interaction API synchronize query parameters for widgets using `bind="query-params"`. Currently, `.set_value(...).run()` changes the widget value but leaves both `at.query_params` and the app's `st.query_params` unchanged, so tests observe a different state from the browser.

### Why?

Native query-param binding lets apps replace manual URL callbacks. After that change, AppTest tests that verify shareable filters or inspect `st.query_params` can no longer reproduce the state reached by the same user interaction in the browser. Each test must manually mirror the binding's serialization into `at.query_params`.

The following self-contained example demonstrates the gap on Streamlit 1.65.0; it also occurs on 1.64.0:

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

st.selectbox("FC", ["A", "B"], key="fc", bind="query-params")
st.session_state["seen_query"] = dict(st.query_params)
""").run()

at.selectbox[0].set_value("B").run()
assert not at.exception
print("Widget:", at.selectbox[0].value)
print("AppTest query params:", at.query_params)
print("App query params:", at.session_state["seen_query"])
```

Save as `repro_query_binding.py` and run `python repro_query_binding.py` with `streamlit==1.65.0` installed. No pytest or app-specific dependencies are required.

Observed:

```text
Widget: B
AppTest query params: {}
App query params: {}
```

In a browser, selecting B in the app string above updates the URL to `?fc=B` and the script sees `{"fc": "B"}`. The same AppTest gap occurs with `st.text_input(..., key="fc", bind="query-params")` and `at.text_input[0].set_value("B").run()`.

### How?

Use the existing interaction API to model the bound query-param update when a widget commits a value. For the example above, the desired result after `.set_value("B").run()` is:

```text
Widget: B
AppTest query params: {'fc': 'B'}
App query params: {'fc': 'B'}
```

The interaction should send a coherent widget-state/query-string pair using the widget's binding semantics, including serialization and clearing of the bound parameter. Unrelated query parameters should remain intact. This can be supported in the existing browserless AppTest API; a new browser runner is not requested.

A current workaround is to set the query params manually in the test before the run:

```python
at.selectbox[0].set_value("B")
at.query_params["fc"] = "B"
at.run()
assert at.session_state["seen_query"]["fc"] == "B"
```

This works, but the test must duplicate application binding logic. Keeping explicit `on_change` callbacks that write `st.query_params` also works, at the cost of retaining the application glue that native binding could replace.

### Additional Context

#### Environment and controls

- Streamlit: 1.65.0, also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python: 3.14.8.
- OS: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest example. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS and confirmed correct binding on both versions.
- The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes; no installed source was modified.
- Initial URL values correctly seed a bound widget in AppTest.
- Programmatically changing `st.session_state["fc"]` before rendering the bound widget correctly updates query params.
- Manual URL-writing callbacks work in AppTest.

#### Related work checked

- [#16906](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16906) requests a first-party browser-testing API. This request targets bound-widget query serialization during existing AppTest interactions.
- [PR #17191](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17191), included in 1.65.0, fixes single-value/list representation in `at.query_params`. The example still returns an empty dict after that fix.
- [PR #16998](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16998) fixes browser back/forward restoration. This example changes a widget through AppTest and performs no history navigation.

I did not find an existing issue requesting this specific AppTest behavior. I am using the feature-request form because this extends the test simulation; the runtime binding itself works in the tested browser examples.

[LocalScriptRunner.run](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/local_script_runner.py#L170) constructs the query string from the query params passed by AppTest. The current widget interaction path does not generate the corresponding query-param update that a browser would send.

comments_data.body:
This is an enhancement to the browserless `AppTest` API. On Streamlit 1.64 and 1.65, `.set_value(...).run()` on a widget with `bind="query-params"` updates the widget value and leaves both `at.query_params` and the app's `st.query_params` empty, while the same selection in the browser sets the URL (for example `?fc=B`). In the browser, `WidgetStateManager.maybeSyncValueToUrl` writes that query string before the rerun, and the next script run receives it as `RerunData.query_string`. `AppTest` only sends the pending widget protobuf from `ElementTree.run` and reuses the current `at.query_params` when `LocalScriptRunner.run` builds that query string. Backend binding in `SessionState.register_widget` seeds widgets from the URL and writes query params back for programmatic `st.session_state` assignments; an incoming widget-state value is treated as already winning, so it is not copied into the URL. Element protos already carry `query_param_key`, so this can stay in the existing AppTest path and should keep unrelated parameters, clear a parameter when the value matches the widget default, and use the same serialization as the frontend.

### Related Issues

- [#16906](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16906) — Requests a Playwright-based `streamlit.testing.e2e` API. A real browser would already apply this URL sync; this issue asks the existing `AppTest` interaction API to emit the bound query string without a browser.
- [#16055](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16055) — Documents that `bind="query-params"` omits a value from the URL when it equals the widget default. An AppTest sync needs that same clear-at-default rule (`WidgetStateManager.shouldClearUrlParam`).
- [#14224](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14224) — Covers how selectbox query values are serialized from `format_func`. AppTest would need the same URL encoding the frontend uses when it writes the bound parameter.

---
