title: Add a first-party Playwright-based e2e testing API (`streamlit.testing.e2e`) alongside AppTest
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a first-party, Playwright-based **end-to-end (browser) testing API** for Streamlit apps — `streamlit.testing.e2e` — as an optional `streamlit[testing]` extra, complementing the existing browserless unit-testing API (`AppTest`). It would provide a Streamlit-aware semantic facade for finding and operating elements in a real browser, rerun/navigation-aware synchronization, useful failure artifacts, and an escape hatch to native Playwright `Page`/`Locator`. Design thoughts are in the [app testing toolkit spec (PR #16041)](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16041).

### Why?

Today users face an unhelpful choice: `AppTest` is fast and Python-native but runs no real frontend (so it can disagree with a real app, and can't cover rendering, custom components, accessibility, media, charts, or real user journeys), while browser testing can validate the real product but Streamlit provides **no supported way** to start the app, wait for reruns, select elements, collect logs, or test a deployed/embedded app — users must assemble and maintain all that infrastructure. Streamlit's own mature `e2e_playwright/` suite solves these hard problems (process lifecycle, ephemeral ports, app-idle detection, traces, iframes, uploads, dataframes/charts, etc.) but is coupled to the repo layout and private DOM test IDs, so it isn't a releasable public API.

This is especially costly for **AI coding agents**, which need a deterministic run command, semantic element identity, a compact description of the current UI, and actionable failure artifacts to validate their work — indexes, private CSS/test IDs, sleeps, and screenshots alone make brittle tests.

### How?

Ship a two-layer testing story with clear boundaries (don't build a third UI-testing engine, and don't turn AppTest into a browser emulator):

- **AppTest (browserless)** stays the fast option for logic/state/basic widget workflows — with improved runtime fidelity and typed + universal semantic queries (`get_by_key`/`get_by_label`/`get_by_text`) and a compact `snapshot()`.
- **`streamlit.testing.e2e` (browser)** — the new Playwright-based API, installed via `pip install "streamlit[testing]"`.

Proposed shape (from the spec):

```python
from playwright.sync_api import expect
from streamlit.testing.e2e import StreamlitPage, app_fixture

app = app_fixture("app.py")

def test_sign_in(app: StreamlitPage):
    app.get_element_by_label("Username", type="text_input").set_value("ada")
    app.get_element_by_label("Password", type="text_input").set_value("correct horse battery staple")
    app.get_element_by_label("Sign in", type="button").click()

    welcome = app.get_element_by_text("Welcome, ada", type="heading")
    expect(welcome.locator).to_be_visible()
```

Key capabilities:
- **App lifecycle fixture:** `app_fixture()` starts one app server per test module on an ephemeral localhost port, gives an isolated browser page per test, and waits until the initial run is idle. Also target direct/external URLs (deployed/embedded apps).
- **Semantic selection:** strict, retrying finders that understand Streamlit elements and layout containers — `get_element_by_key` / `get_element_by_label` / `get_element_by_text`, plus `get_element(type=...)` / `get_elements(type=...)`; a returned element that is a container (sidebar, form, expander, popover, dialog, tab, column, container) can scope further queries. An optional `type` discriminator maps to a generated public `ElementType` taxonomy for IDE completion.
- **Rerun/navigation-aware synchronization** so tests don't rely on sleeps.
- **Actionable failure artifacts** (text/logs/traces/screenshots) and a **semantic snapshot** (`semantic_snapshot()`) as a token-efficient interface for humans and agents.
- **Escape hatch** to native Playwright `Page`/`Locator` for anything the facade doesn't cover.
- A shared **testability vocabulary** across both layers (public element types, labels, keys, containers), explicitly optimized for AI agents.

### Additional Context

- Spec: [PR #16041 — \`[spec] Streamlit app testing toolkit\`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16041) (`specs/2026-07-16-streamlit-app-testing-toolkit/product-spec.md`).
- Related: open `feature:app-testing` issues, e.g. #9786, #13163, #9128.

title: Add page and app descriptions (`page_description`, `st.Page`, `st.App`)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add first-class authored descriptions at the page and app level: `page_description` on `st.set_page_config`, optionally `description` on `st.Page`, and a static title + description on `st.App`. Today a page can declare a title and icon, and an app has no catalog-level identity at all — so SEO, assistive tech, navigation, and non-browser clients all have to infer meaning from body copy.

### Why?

A Streamlit page already has `page_title` / `title` and `page_icon` / `icon`. There is no matching place to say what the page or the app *is*. Authors stuff that into `st.caption`, `st.markdown`, or `menu_items["About"]`, none of which is structured metadata.

That gap shows up in several places that all want the same authored sentence:

- **SEO and link previews.** Search and social crawlers need a description (and today only Community Cloud injects sharing tags). Related: #16634, #6567, #2469, #9058.
- **Accessibility.** A document-level description is the page analogue of alt text (#8563 covers elements; this is the page/app layer).
- **Multipage navigation.** `st.Page` can name a page but cannot explain it, so a nav list or catalog cannot tell "Regional revenue" from "Reports" without running the page.
- **Non-browser clients.** An agent snapshot currently serializes `url_path`, `title`, and `icon` only. A static app descriptor should be able to return title + description *without executing app code* — which is why the app-level fields belong on `st.App`, not only inside the script.

### How?

**Page description on `st.set_page_config`**, matching `page_title` / `page_icon`:

```python
st.set_page_config(
    page_title="Regional revenue",
    page_icon=":material/payments:",
    page_description=(
        "Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds. Periods are UTC."
    ),
)
```

**Optional `description` on `st.Page`**, so the page list carries copy without running each page (consistent with `title` / `icon`, not `page_*`):

```python
st.Page(
    "revenue.py",
    title="Regional revenue",
    icon=":material/payments:",
    description="Net revenue by billing region. Excludes refunds.",
)
```

**Static title and description on `st.App`**, available without executing the script:

```python
app = st.App(
    "main.py",
    title="Finance apps",
    description=(
        "Internal finance dashboards. Net revenue excludes refunds and is in EUR."
    ),
)
```

Suggested behavior:

- `st.Page.description` is the default for that page; `st.set_page_config(page_description=...)` overrides it for the current run (same additive pattern as today's page title).
- Single-page apps that never call `st.Page` still get a description via `set_page_config`.
- `st.App` title/description are app-level and static. They do not replace per-page title/description. For `streamlit run` apps without `st.App`, the default page's title/description (or a future config option) can stand in.
- Consumers of the same strings: HTML `<meta name="description">` / Open Graph, assistive tech, navigation (if we choose to surface it), and structured snapshots / a static app descriptor.

**Naming.** `page_description` on `set_page_config` matches `page_title`. On `st.Page` and `st.App`, `description` / `title` match the existing `title` parameter (the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) also floated `app_title` / `app_description` on `st.App` if we want the prefix explicit).

**Not in this request:** element-level alternative text for images, charts, and tables (#8563) and `help` on media (#3133). Arbitrary extra `<meta>` tags (GSC verification, etc.) stay with #16634.

### Additional Context

- Suggested as a standalone follow-up in the [agent-app interface spec](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/docs/agent-app-interface/specs/2026-08-28-agent-app-interface/product-spec.md) ([#16843](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16843), follow-up #3): apps should explain themselves in authored metadata, not only in body widgets. Worth doing on accessibility and SEO merits even without the agent interface.
- Related:
  - #16634 — inject `<meta>` tags; a first-class `page_description` is the content those tags would publish, not a general meta-tag API
  - #6567 — social sharing meta tags outside Community Cloud
  - #2469 (closed) — `st.set_page_config(description=...)`
  - #9058 — title/favicon in the initial HTML (same "available before JS" problem)
  - #8563 — element-level alt text
  - #5673 (closed) — config-file website metadata

title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
body:
### Summary

When a Components V2 component calls `setTriggerValue` during mount (inside the default function, rather than from a user event handler), values are silently lost if the component remounts because its `data` changed — even when an explicit `key` is passed, which keeps the element id stable.

Measured roughly a quarter loss: **5 of 21 values sent were never received by Python at all.** They are not late — a scan of the entire session log shows they never arrive in any subsequent run.

This is split out of #14710, where it surfaced during investigation. It is distinct from the two by-design mechanisms discussed there (`data` participating in element identity for unkeyed components, and trigger values resetting after each run).

**Update — measured root cause.** A frontend race in `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive`: it destroys the synthetic trigger-aggregator widget state while that state is still awaiting its batched flush, so the app reruns with no trigger at all. Not a backend discard. Measured on a production build with the repro below: 10/85 values lost unpatched vs 0/85 patched, and with instrumentation, 14/14 losses correlated exactly with the destroying call. Mechanism and open question under Additional Information.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

comp = st.components.v2.component(
    "repro.mount_trigger",
    js="""
    export default function (component) {
        const v = "val" + component.data.nonce;
        console.log("SEND " + v);
        component.setTriggerValue("v", v);
    }
    """,
)

if "clicks" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.clicks = 0
if st.button("bump"):
    st.session_state.clicks += 1

nonce = f"c{st.session_state.clicks}"
result = comp(data={"nonce": nonce}, key="stable_key")

received = result.get("v")
st.write(f"data nonce {nonce} -> received {received!r}")
print(f"nonce={nonce} received={received!r}", flush=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and open the browser console.
2. Click **bump** ~20 times, letting the app settle between clicks. Each click changes `data`, so the component remounts and sends one value.
3. Compare the `SEND val…` lines in the console against the `received=…` lines in the terminal.
4. Roughly one in four sent values never appears on the Python side.

### Expected Behavior

Every value the mounted component sends is readable on the following script run. The explicit `key` makes the element id stable, so a changing `data` payload should not affect delivery.

### Current Behavior

About 25% of values are never delivered. Verified as lost rather than late by scanning the full backend log after all clicks — 0 arrived in a later run.

The element id was logged each run and confirmed identical throughout (`$$ID-b4c118c7288cf7d656c205e58a384db6-stable_key`), so this is not the identity churn that affects unkeyed components.

Three controls on the same harness came out clean. They do not isolate the bug to trigger-on-mount — see Additional Information — but they do narrow which write path is affected:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| `setStateValue` on mount, same conditions | 21/21 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, stable `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, churning `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| **`setTriggerValue` on mount, churning `data`** | **5 of 21 lost** |

### Additional Information

**Mechanism.** `setTriggerValue` writes to a synthetic aggregator widget id (`makeTriggerAggregatorId` → `$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<componentId>__events`) and the flush is deferred to a `setTimeout(…, 0)` macrotask. `App.removeInactiveWidgetState()` runs from the `ScriptFinished` → `clearStaleNodes` setState callback and deletes every widget state whose id is not an active *element* id — the aggregator id never is, because it isn't part of the element tree. When that lands before the flush, the trigger is deleted but the rerun is still sent (`sendUpdateWidgetsMessage` uses unfiltered `createWidgetStatesMsg()`), so the script reruns with no trigger.

Mount-time triggers are the most exposed path: the component's `default function` runs behind `await loadAndRunModule(...)` (dynamic `import()` of a blob URL), so it executes a macrotask or more after the commit that mounted it. This also explains the control table — `setStateValue` is immune because it writes the component's real element id, and the event-handler controls passed because letting the app settle means `removeInactive` has already run.

**The `_pending_resets` theory is ruled out.** It is only populated by `mark_page_switch_drops`, which runs on page transitions and skips widgets whose recorded page is the current page, so a single-page app never populates it. (For the record, the original hypothesis was that `_pending_resets` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py` discarded a frontend-resent value on re-registration, which would have made this by design.)

**Related blind spot.** The same synthetic id is invisible to other active-id filters, not just this one: `App.tsx` `onPageChange` sends `getActiveWidgetStates(activeWidgetIds)`, which would likewise drop a pending aggregator. Reaching it would require a trigger and a page navigation in the same macrotask, and dropping a trigger while navigating away is defensible, so no change is planned there. Recorded as an observation only.

**Scope of what was tested.** Measured against this repro on one machine, 235 trials total. It establishes this race as the cause of the loss seen here; it does not rule out other trigger-loss paths. The same race also appears to explain the recurring `bidi_components/basics_test.py::test_trigger_interactions` CI flake — the failure signature (counts unchanged plus `Result` reset to `None`) is what a trigger-less rerun produces — but that link is inferred from the signature, not directly observed. Two prior automated PRs (#14542, #14843) misattributed that flake to a slow iframe round-trip and raised timeouts.

**Open question for Components V2** (replacing the original question here, which is now answered — the drop is a race, not intentional): should `setTriggerValue` during mount be a supported pattern at all? Fixing the race makes it reliable, but it fires on every remount, so churning `data` produces one trigger per remount. That is a semantics decision independent of this bug, and it determines whether this issue closes as fixed or splits into a fix plus a documentation/warning change.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (released wheel, production frontend build)
- Python version: 3.11 · macOS · Chromium
- The ~25% figure is one 21-trial sample on a single machine; treat it as "roughly a quarter" rather than a precise rate.

comments_data.body:
This is a real Components V2 race, not identity churn and almost certainly not `_pending_resets`. With an explicit `key`, the element id stays stable (`key_as_main_identity=True`), but `useHandleJsContent` still re-runs the default export whenever `data` changes. A mount-time `setTriggerValue` then has to win a one-shot delivery race: the value is stored under the synthetic trigger-aggregator id (`$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<id>__events`), flushed on `setTimeout(0)`, deleted from client widget state, and cleared again by `_reset_triggers()` at the end of every script run.

That aggregator id is not in the render tree, so `removeInactiveWidgetState()` on `ScriptFinished` can delete a pending trigger before the macrotask flush sends it. `_coalesce_widget_states` also preserves `trigger_value` / `chat_input_value` across queued reruns but not `json_trigger_value`, so a second widget-update message can overwrite a just-queued CCv2 trigger. Both fit the controls: `setStateValue` lives on the element id and persists; event-handler triggers fire after the app has settled. `_pending_resets` is page-scope persist-state tracking and is not involved in this repro.

Mount-time triggers are still a poor fit for Streamlit's model (use `setStateValue` for init data), but silent ~25% loss with a stable key is a bug, not intended discard-on-re-register.

### Related Issues

- [#14710](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14710) — Parent investigation this was split from. Most of that report is by-design (unkeyed `data` in identity, trigger reset after each run, first-run empty result). This issue is the remaining genuine drop with a stable `key`.
- [#8041](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8041) — Older Components V1 “not ready on first load / retry” request. Same class of mount-time value timing, different API.
- [#10102](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10102) — Another execution-model race around reruns and widget values (`fastReruns` / delayed script). Not CCv2-specific, but the same “in-flight rerun vs widget state” family.

title: Add a developer debug pane for inspecting state, cache, memory, and profiling
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a built-in developer "debug pane" — a panel (e.g. a collapsible sidebar/overlay) that surfaces debug information and dev tools without cluttering the main app. It would visualize `st.session_state` and cache contents, show memory usage and profiling/performance info, and provide a place to dump debug output (`st.help`, variables, etc.). By default it would be visible only to the app developer (not viewers), so developers don't have to comment debug code in and out.

### Why?

Debugging Streamlit apps today means peppering the main UI with `st.write(st.session_state)`, `st.help(...)`, timing prints, etc., then remembering to remove them. There's no first-class way to inspect what's actually going on — state, cache, memory, timings — in a dedicated, developer-only surface. A debug pane (à la [Django Debug Toolbar](https://github.com/jazzband/django-debug-toolbar)) would make development and troubleshooting dramatically easier and keep debug output out of the real app for end users.

### How?

A developer-only container/panel that is disabled by default for viewers other than the app developer. Over time it could host focused tools, for example:

- **State inspector:** visualize `st.session_state` contents.
- **Cache inspector:** visualize `st.cache_data` / `st.cache_resource` contents (and allow clearing).
- **Memory profiling:** memory usage, and how it changes run-over-run.
- **Execution/performance profiling:** time between/within widget calls and functions; distribution of run times run-over-run (e.g. via a profiler like yappi + a viewer like snakeviz).
- **Debug output container:** a scratch area to write `st.help`, dump variables, etc., that doesn't appear in the main window.
- **Variable inspector:** e.g. a selectbox + `st.help`.
- **Element/DOM inspector:** which widgets were rendered, and their inputs/values; last forward/back message (or equivalent).
- **Console logs** and **error context**.
- Possibly a **Python console** at the end of the app to run quick calculations/inspections (like a Jupyter interactive debugger).

Considerations:
- Developer-only visibility by default (not shown to app viewers); tie into a development vs. production mode.
- Start minimal (state + cache inspection) and grow over time.

### Additional Context

- Prior art: [Django Debug Toolbar](https://github.com/jazzband/django-debug-toolbar), [streamlit-forum](https://github.com/snehankekre/streamlit-forum).
- Closely related: #16306 (dedicated development and production modes) — this debug pane is a natural home for the "development mode" dev tools described there.

title: Deprecate widget callback `args`/`kwargs` in favor of `functools.partial`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Deprecate the `args` and `kwargs` parameters that widgets currently expose for passing arguments to `on_change` / `on_click` callbacks, and recommend `functools.partial` instead. As part of this, support automatically receiving relevant state (e.g. the widget's new value) in the callback, as requested in #5305.

### Why?

- **Redundant API surface:** `args`/`kwargs` exist on essentially every widget purely to forward arguments to callbacks. Python already has a standard, well-understood tool for this — `functools.partial` — so `args`/`kwargs` are extra parameters to learn, document, and maintain on every widget for something the language handles natively.
- **Consistency & simplicity:** removing them shrinks the signature of every widget and aligns with "prefer Pythonic idioms" and "extend/compose over inventing".
- **Better ergonomics for callbacks:** today callbacks often have to read `st.session_state` to find out what value changed, which makes generic reusable handlers awkward. Passing the value (and possibly key) to the callback automatically (#5305) removes that friction.

### How?

- **Recommend `functools.partial`** as the replacement for `args`/`kwargs`:

```python
from functools import partial

def update(param_name, *, value):
    ...

st.selectbox("Pick", options, on_change=partial(update, "selection_1"))
```

- **Deprecate `args`/`kwargs`** on widgets with a long, clearly-communicated deprecation window and docs/migration guidance (they keep working during the deprecation period). See API principle "Graceful Evolution" (3+ months notice, clear migration path).
- **Auto-pass state to callbacks** (#5305): make the widget's new value available to the callback automatically (e.g. as a keyword argument), so reusable/generic handlers don't need to reach into `st.session_state`. The exact mechanism needs design (opt-in signature detection vs. a fixed kwarg) to stay backwards compatible.

### Additional Context

- Incorporates #5305 (pass state as a parameter to the `on_change` callback).
- This is a cross-cutting change affecting all widgets with callbacks (`on_change`/`on_click`), so it warrants a spec and careful, gradual deprecation.

title: Minimize `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` errors
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Reduce how often developers hit `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` (duplicate widget/element ID) errors by making element ID generation smarter about the surrounding container context — so that identical widgets placed in different containers (chat messages, fragments, columns, etc.) don't collide without the developer having to manually craft unique `key`s everywhere.

### Why?

It's increasingly common to have repeating identical widgets across different chat messages, fragment calls, or columns. Today the developer must manage and track a unique `key` for each, which adds a lot of boilerplate and complexity. This is especially painful in chat/LLM apps (in-chat interactive widgets, code-eval "run" buttons, generated suggestion buttons) — and for LLM-generated code it can be nearly impossible to solve, since the model may emit duplicate widgets across messages. `st.form` already avoids this within forms (the `form_id` is part of the ID), which shows the approach can work more broadly.

This is a high-impact papercut: `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` is the **No. 3 most thrown uncaught exception type**, occurring in ~**0.5% of all apps**.

A related pain point: some elements raise `StreamlitDuplicateElementId` and tell you to add a `key`, but **don't actually support a `key` argument**, leaving no clean fix. Examples:
- #11424 — showing the same `st.plotly_chart` multiple times raises `StreamlitDuplicateElementId`.
- #11360 — multiple `st.audio` calls with the same parameters and `autoplay=True` raise a duplicate error that prompts you to add a key, but `st.audio` has no `key`.

### How?

Incorporate more of the container context into an element's ID computation, focusing on **stable, explicit signals** (not user-facing text). Ideas:

- **Wrapping container keys:** automatically include the `key` of wrapping containers / `st.fragment` / `st.form` (those that support keys) in the child element's ID computation. Only for containers that have an explicit key set.
  - If we do this, it strengthens the case for **adding `key` to more containers and elements** — see #9580 and the concrete cases #11424 (`st.plotly_chart`) and #11360 (`st.audio`), plus #6152.
- **Re-evaluate key namespaces and parent-key reuse:** regular element keys, form IDs, and fragment definition keys are currently tracked in separate registries. `st.form` already contributes its `form_id` to the auto-generated IDs of unkeyed children; fragment keys identify fragment definitions but are not currently part of regular child element ID computation. Consider both:
  - Reusing explicit form / fragment / keyed-container keys as stable parent context for **unkeyed** descendants.
  - Whether form and fragment keys should participate in the same duplicate-key checks as regular element keys, or remain separate namespaces that only contribute parent context.

  Treat registry unification as a compatibility decision: the same string can currently be reused between some form / fragment and regular-element keys, and one keyed fragment definition can intentionally run from multiple call sites. Preserve the rule that an explicit child `key` is authoritative and independent of its container.
- **Column index in `st.columns`:** include the column number in the ID computation so the same widget in different columns of the same `st.columns` call doesn't collide.
- **Parent container types:** include the parent container type(s) as part of the ID computation.

**Important caution — be conservative about what goes into ID generation.** Adding container context to the ID changes element identity, which has a subtle downside: a widget that **dynamically moves between containers** (e.g. its wrapping container changes across reruns) would get a new ID and thus lose its identity and state. This is the main risk to weigh (more so than existing widget state resetting on upgrade), and it can be fixed by explicitly setting a `key` on that element so its identity no longer depends on the container context. In particular:
- **Do not** include user-facing **labels/titles** of wrapping containers (e.g. expander label, dialog title, popover label, tab name) in the ID — these change often and would be fragile/surprising. Prefer **explicitly set keys** for disambiguation instead.
- Auto-added context must apply **only to widgets without an explicit `key`**. When a user sets an explicit `key="x"`, the ID must **not** include the added container context — an explicit key should always behave predictably and stay stable regardless of the surrounding containers. Think through backwards compatibility / migration carefully.

### Additional Context

- Add `key` to more elements/containers: #9580, and concrete duplicate-ID cases where no `key` is available today: #11424 (`st.plotly_chart`), #11360 (`st.audio`).
- Related: #6152 (composable/reusable component API for larger apps).
- `st.form` already includes `form_id` in widget ID generation — a useful precedent.
- There is an older internal product spec exploring options (implicit container key-prefix, adding `key`/`key_prefix` to containers, best-practice docs, or fixing duplicate IDs via enumeration). This issue intentionally leans toward the conservative, explicit-key-based approaches from that discussion.

title: Nested run_every fragment stays on screen with stale content after being hidden
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a nested `run_every` fragment stops being rendered, its container can stay on screen showing frozen, stale content until the *enclosing* fragment next completes a run. Because the enclosing fragment has no timer of its own, that means it stays visible until the user next interacts with it.

The cause is on the frontend: the enclosing fragment's run finishes successfully and schedules the usual stale-node cleanup, but that cleanup executes with a *later* run's `scriptRunId`/`fragmentIdsThisRun`, so it is scoped to the wrong fragment and never prunes the evicted subtree.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from uuid import uuid4

import streamlit as st


@st.fragment(run_every=1.0)
def standalone_auto():
    with st.container(key="standalone_auto_fragment"):
        st.write(f"uuid in fragment: {uuid4()}")


standalone_auto()


@st.fragment
def outer():
    show_nested = st.checkbox("Show nested auto fragment", value=True)
    if show_nested:

        @st.fragment
        def middle():
            @st.fragment(run_every=1.0)
            def nested_auto():
                with st.container(key="nested_auto_fragment"):
                    st.write(f"nested uuid: {uuid4()}")

            nested_auto()

        middle()


outer()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above and wait a few seconds so both `run_every` fragments are ticking.
2. Uncheck "Show nested auto fragment".
3. Repeat, toggling at varying moments relative to the 1s tick. Under CPU load it reproduces roughly once every 4-6 attempts; on an idle machine it is rare.

It is timing sensitive: the toggle has to land while the standalone fragment's next auto-rerun is arriving. Note that `console.log`-based instrumentation slows message handling enough to hide it — use an in-page array if you need to trace.

### Expected Behavior

Unchecking the box removes the nested fragment's container, as it does on a normal rerun.

### Current Behavior

The `nested_auto_fragment` container stays in the DOM with its last-rendered content. It does not update again (its auto-rerun timer is correctly cancelled by `stop_auto_rerun`), so it reads as stale data rather than an obviously broken element. It clears on a full rerun, or when the enclosing fragment next completes a run — which for a timer-less fragment means the next user interaction with it.

Also seen in CI as a flake in `st_fragment_run_every_test.py::test_nested_fragment_run_every_can_hide_without_crash` (e.g. https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/actions/runs/33181944052), failing with `Locator expected not to be attached`.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Not a regression of #15130. That fixed the white-screen crash in this same scenario (#15084); this leftover-element behavior is a separate defect in the same area.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`)
- Python version: 3.11.6
- Operating System: macOS 26.6.2
- Browser: reproduced on WebKit; not browser specific

### Additional Information

**Root cause (verified by instrumenting the frontend).** `handleScriptFinished` schedules stale-node cleanup inside a `setState` updater that reads `scriptRunId` and `fragmentIdsThisRun` from `prevState` (`frontend/app/src/App.tsx:2027-2038`). Under load the next fragment run has already been committed by the time that updater flushes, so the cleanup runs for the wrong run. Captured trace, with the scheduling status paired against the state the updater actually saw:

```
delta addBlock   frag=28b54e path=0.1   run=6bd090          <- enclosing fragment writes
delta newElement frag=28b54e path=0.1.0 run=6bd090
scriptFinished ENTRY status=FINISHED_FRAGMENT_RUN_SUCCESSFULLY
                     entryRun=6bd090 entryFrags=28b54e      <- its run, finished successfully
delta ... frag=f81f56 run=af93e8                            <- next (standalone) run starts
cleanup scheduledBy=FINISHED_FRAGMENT_RUN_SUCCESSFULLY
        SEES run=af93e8 frags=f81f56                        <- executed as the standalone run
```

So the cleanup ran as `clearStaleNodes(af93e8, ["f81f56"])`. `ClearStaleNodeVisitor` therefore never descended into the enclosing fragment's subtree at `0.1` with `fragmentIdOfBlock` set, and the evicted container was never pruned.

Worth noting the run finished `FINISHED_FRAGMENT_RUN_SUCCESSFULLY`, **not** `FINISHED_EARLY_FOR_RERUN` — so this is not the deliberate cleanup skip for interrupted runs.

**Why this probably needs a server-side change.** `ForwardMsg.script_finished` is a bare enum (`proto/streamlit/proto/ForwardMsg.proto:46-57`, `:66`) and carries no run identity, so the client can only infer which run finished from React state. Both readings are unreliable, in opposite directions, and I observed each failing in the same session:

- at flush time it can see a *later* run (the failure above);
- at handler entry it can see an *earlier* run, when several messages are handled before a commit.

Carrying the run id (and `fragment_ids_this_run`) on `ScriptFinished` so cleanup can be pinned to the run that actually finished would fix it at the source.

**One constraint for whoever picks this up.** A frontend-only workaround that *removes* the evicted nodes is unsafe. Deltas address nodes by absolute path, and `AppRoot.addBlock` inherits an existing block's children rather than resetting them, so removing a node compacts its parent's `children` and every later sibling keeps the shifted index. A fragment sibling that reruns on its own then writes to the wrong slot — I reproduced a silent duplication (`["live"]` → later delta at its original path `[0, 1]` → `["live", "live v2"]`), and `SetNodeByDeltaPathVisitor` can escalate the same shift to a `Bad delta path index` throw. Substituting an index-preserving empty block avoids that, but does not address the attribution race itself. Explored in #16705, which is closed in favour of this issue.

**Related:** #15084, #15130 (the crash in this scenario), #10805 (widget-state cleanup with `run_every`).

title: Broken relative link in .github/copilot-instructions.md and stale knip ignoreDependencies entries
body:

### Summary

Two small repository-hygiene defects found while auditing the tree.

**1. Broken relative link in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`**

Line 88 reads:

```markdown
- See [.claude/skills/debugging-streamlit/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/debugging-streamlit/SKILL.md) for the full debugging guide.
```

The file lives in `.github/`, so the relative link resolves to `.github/.claude/skills/debugging-streamlit/SKILL.md`, which does not exist. The real file is at the repository root: `.claude/skills/debugging-streamlit/SKILL.md`.

This text is duplicated from `AGENTS.md`, where the same relative link is correct because that file sits at the root — the copy into `.github/` did not adjust the path.

Fix: use `../.claude/skills/debugging-streamlit/SKILL.md` (or a root-absolute link).

**2. Stale `ignoreDependencies` entries in `frontend/knip.json`**

`yarn knip` reports three entries that are no longer needed:

```
Configuration hints (3)
@deck.gl/extensions          knip.json  Remove from ignoreDependencies
@deck.gl/widgets             knip.json  Remove from ignoreDependencies
react-responsive-carousel    knip.json  Remove from ignoreDependencies
```

These suppressions now hide nothing, so keeping them only reduces the value of the check.

Fix: drop the three entries.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open `.github/copilot-instructions.md` on GitHub and click the link on line 88 — it 404s.
2. Run `yarn knip` in `frontend/` and read the "Configuration hints" section.

### Expected Behavior

- The documentation link resolves to the skill file.
- `yarn knip` reports no configuration hints.

### Current Behavior

- The link 404s.
- Three stale hints are reported on every run.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `yarn knip` reports no configuration hints.

The other candidates were either illustrative syntax examples in the `developing-with-streamlit` skill docs or a spec referencing a path that was never created.

title: st.slider corrupts min_value/max_value when bounds are reversed, silently producing a wrong range
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`_slider()` tries to swap reversed bounds with two sequential statements, but the second one reads the variable the first one just overwrote:

```python
# lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py:1081-1083
# Ensure that min <= value(s) <= max, adjusting the bounds as necessary.
min_value = min(min_value, max_value)
max_value = max(min_value, max_value)   # <-- min_value is already the new (smaller) value
```

After line 1082, `min_value` is `min(a, b)`, so line 1083 evaluates `max(min(a, b), b)`, which is always `b`. The original `min_value` can never become the upper bound, so the intended swap never happens. Depending on what `value` is, this silently produces a wrong range or raises an exception quoting numbers the user never passed.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

# 1. Bounds silently reinterpreted
st.slider("a", 10, 1)                                  # -> range 1..10, value 10

# 2. Upper bound silently invented from `value`
st.slider("b", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=5)     # -> range 1..5  (max_value=1 is gone)

# 3. Spurious exception quoting numbers the user never passed
st.slider("c", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=1)     # -> StreamlitAPIException
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run any of the three lines above.
2. Compare the resulting slider bounds against the arguments passed.

### Expected Behavior

Either of the following would be self-consistent:

- Reject reversed bounds with a clear error naming the two values the caller actually supplied, the way `st.date_input` already does:
  > The `min_value`, set to 2024-01-02, shouldn't be larger than the `max_value`, set to 2024-01-01.
- Or genuinely swap them, so `st.slider("a", 10, 1)` yields a `1..10` slider — which is what the code comment says it intends.

Today it does neither reliably.

### Current Behavior

Verified with `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest`:

```
slider(min=10, max=1)            -> min=1.0 max=10.0 value=10
slider(min=10, max=1, value=5)   -> min=1.0 max=5.0  value=5
slider(min=10, max=1, value=1)   -> RAISED: Slider `min_value` must be less than the `max_value`.
                                            The values were 1 and 1.
```

Note case 3: the user passed `10` and `1`, but the error reports "The values were 1 and 1" — both numbers have been overwritten by the faulty normalization. Case 2 is the most damaging, because it silently produces a slider whose upper bound (`5`) was never supplied as a bound at all; it leaked in from `value`.

Isolating just the two lines:

```python
min_value, max_value = 10, 1
min_value = min(min_value, max_value)
max_value = max(min_value, max_value)
print(min_value, max_value)   # 1 1     <-- current behavior

min_value, max_value = 10, 1
min_value, max_value = min(min_value, max_value), max(min_value, max_value)
print(min_value, max_value)   # 1 10    <-- intended
```

The `min_value == max_value` guard at line 1137 then fires on values that are an artifact of this bug rather than of user input, and it only catches the case where the corruption happens to collapse both bounds to the same number — which is why `st.slider("x", 5, 5)` errors while `st.slider("x", 10, 1)` does not.

### Suggested Fix

Assign both bounds simultaneously (or compute the max from the original value):

```python
min_value, max_value = min(min_value, max_value), max(min_value, max_value)
```

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `st.slider("b", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=5)` no longer produces a slider whose upper bound came from `value`.
- [ ] Reversed bounds either swap correctly or raise an error that quotes the values the caller actually passed.
- [ ] Test coverage for reversed `min_value`/`max_value` with `value` below, inside, and above the range.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Unknown.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11 (logic is platform-independent)
- Browser: n/a (reproduced headlessly via `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest`)

### Additional Information

Related but distinct: #5099 covers `value` falling outside `(min_value, max_value)`. This report is specifically about the bound-normalization statements corrupting `min_value`/`max_value` themselves.

title: Modernize Streamlit's default light and dark themes
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Refresh Streamlit's built-in default light and dark themes to feel more modern and polished out of the box — updated colors, typography, spacing, radii, and component styling — so that apps look great by default without custom theming.

### Why?

The default look is what every new app and most demos ship with, so it strongly shapes the perception of Streamlit. The current defaults feel somewhat dated compared to modern design systems (e.g. shadcn, Tailwind, Tremor, Material 3). A refreshed, cohesive default theme would make apps look more professional immediately, improve the first impression for new users, and reduce how often people reach for custom CSS/themes just to look current.

### How?

Revisit the default theme tokens and component styling for both light and dark modes, for example:

- **Color palette:** refined neutrals/grays, a more modern primary color, and better semantic colors (success/warning/error/info) with good contrast in both modes.
- **Dark mode:** ensure it's a first-class, well-balanced theme (not just an inversion) — proper surface elevations, borders, and contrast.
- **Typography:** modern default font, refined sizes/weights/line-heights and hierarchy.
- **Spacing & shape:** consistent spacing scale and slightly softer, contemporary border radii and borders.
- **Components:** cohesive styling across widgets, containers, dataframes, charts, etc.

Considerations:
- Accessibility: maintain/improve WCAG contrast in both themes.
- Backwards compatibility: this changes the look of existing apps, so consider how to roll it out (e.g. a new theme version/opt-in, migration notes) to avoid surprising users.
- Keep it fully overridable via the existing `[theme]` config.

### Additional Context

- Inspiration: modern design systems like shadcn/ui, Tailwind, Tremor, and Material 3.

title: A custom component cannot own the `r` or `c` keys: the app-level shortcuts fire regardless
body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary Streamlit's `r` (rerun) and `c` (clear cache) shortcuts fire whenever focus is on anything other than a small set of native form elements. A custom component that binds those keys cannot keep them: even a capture-phase listener calling `preventDefault()`, `stopPropagation()` and `stopImmediatePropagation()` sees the key and the app still acts on it. This makes single-letter keyboard interfaces — the norm in accessible visualization libraries, where a blind user drives a chart from the keyboard — impossible to build on Streamlit's non-iframe component path. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python # app.py import streamlit as st st.session_state["runs"] = st.session_state.get("runs", 0) + 1 st.write(f"RUNS={st.session_state['runs']}") st.text_input("a text input") st.button("a button") st.markdown( '
' "a custom widget
", unsafe_allow_html=True, ) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Save the snippet above as `app.py` and run `streamlit run app.py`. 2. Click the bordered div to focus it, press r, and watch `RUNS` increment. 3. To confirm a component cannot defend the key, run this in the browser console and press r again with the div focused: ```js document.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'r') { e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation(); } }, true); // capture phase — the earliest a listener can run ``` ### Expected Behavior A component should be able to opt out of app-level key handling for the region it owns, or the exemption should extend to focus inside a registered custom component. ### Current Behavior The capture-phase listener above receives the event, and the app reruns anyway. Measured on **Streamlit 1.61.1**, driving a real browser and checking whether the app acted: | focused element | `r` | `c` | |---|---|---| | page body | app acts | app acts | | `
` | **app acts** | **app acts** | | `

title: Altair/Vega-Lite native toolbar: hover the download icon to choose PNG or SVG
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

After Altair/Vega-Lite charts started using the native Streamlit toolbar, clicking the download icon next to Fullscreen saves a PNG only. Please keep that native download icon, and on hover show a small toolbar-styled dropdown so the user can choose PNG or SVG.

### Why?

I'm always frustrated when I hover an Altair/Vega-Lite chart, see the native download icon beside Fullscreen, click it, and can only get PNG.

For reports and papers I often need SVG (vector, scalable) as well as PNG. The old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu offered "Save as PNG" / "Save as SVG". After https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15806, that menu is gone, SVG export is gone, and `usermeta.embedOptions` can no longer restore export actions.

Workarounds (custom HTML components, extra `st.download_button`s, or DOM hacks) either leave the native toolbar unused or drift out of style as Streamlit's toolbar design changes. There is no public API to attach a format menu to the existing toolbar download button.

Related but different: #8177 is about PNG resolution, not choosing a format.

### How?

Keep the existing native download icon on Altair/Vega-Lite (and other Vega) charts, in the same toolbar row as Fullscreen.

When the pointer hovers that download icon, show a compact dropdown that matches the toolbar (same icon size, radius, colors, light/dark theme). Suggested items:

- Download PNG
- Download SVG

Clicking an item exports from the current Vega view (`toImageURL("png")` / `toImageURL("svg")`) and starts a browser download.

A click with no menu selection can keep today's PNG-only behavior as the default.

I do not need a new `st` command. Optional later: `st.altair_chart(..., download_formats=("png", "svg"))` to choose which items appear. A Python API is nice-to-have; the hover menu on the native icon is the main request.

Please do not bring back the old Vega-Embed ⋯ menu (View Source / Open in Vega Editor). This should stay a Streamlit toolbar control.

### Additional Context

- Native toolbar change that removed SVG: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15806
- Older embedOptions / actions discussion: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/does-altairs-set-embed-options-work-with-streamlit/1675
- PNG quality (related, not this request): https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8177

I am building a Streamlit questionnaire analysis app that shows many static Altair charts. Users expect the hover toolbar download icon (same family as Fullscreen) to let them pick PNG vs SVG, without a separate download widget beside every chart.

title: Add a `type="cards"` variant to `st.radio` for a card/bordered design
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.radio` with a `"cards"` variant that renders each option as a bordered, selectable card (with the selected card highlighted) instead of the default radio-button list. Same widget behavior — only the visual style changes. See [Tremor's Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group) for the look.

### Why?

Card-style single-select is a very common, more prominent and touch-friendly pattern for choosing between a few richer options (e.g. plans, payment methods, layouts, modes). Today users approximate it with columns + bordered containers + buttons/`st.radio` and a lot of manual state/CSS work. A built-in `"cards"` variant makes this polished pattern a one-liner.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
choice = st.radio(
    "Choose a plan",
    ["Starter", "Pro", "Enterprise"],
    captions=[
        "For individuals getting started",
        "For growing teams",
        "Advanced controls & support",
    ],
    type="cards",
)
```

- `type="default"` — current radio-button list.
- `type="cards"` — render each option as a bordered card; the selected option is visually highlighted.
- Keep existing params working (`captions`, `horizontal`, `format_func`, `index=None`, etc.). Captions map naturally to a description line inside each card.

**Alternative solution — a `border: bool` parameter:** Instead of a `type` enum, just add `st.radio(..., border=True)` that wraps each option in a bordered card. This mirrors the `border` parameter on `st.container` and keeps the API minimal. Downside: it's less extensible than a `type` enum if we later want more visual variants (e.g. `"pills"`), and it's a boolean rather than a named style.

### Additional Context

- Reference designs:
  - [Tremor — Radio Card Group](https://www.tremor.so/docs/inputs/radio-card-group)
  - [Tailwind Plus — Radio Groups (card designs)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/forms/radio-groups)
  - [streamlit-extras — Card Selector](https://extras.streamlit.app/?extra=%F0%9F%83%8F+Card+Selector) (existing community implementation)
- Related: #2325 (`st.radio` with sections), #7184 (stretch horizontal radio), #11959 (consistent API for selectbox/pills/segmented_control/radio).

comments_data.body:
Enhancement request to add an optional `type` parameter to `st.radio` (`"default"` | `"cards"`) so options can render as bordered, selectable cards (Tremor-style radio card group) while keeping existing radio semantics and params (`captions`, `horizontal`, `format_func`, etc.). This is a visual/presentation variant, not a new selection model; users currently approximate it with columns, borders, buttons, and custom CSS. No exact duplicate was found among open issues.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12255 — Asks for a larger, more prominent `st.segmented_control` for high-level single-select; same product need for a more card-like / touch-friendly choice UI, but on a different widget.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7184 — Horizontal `st.radio` layout/styling request (full-width stretch); related `st.radio` presentation enhancement, not a cards variant.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16481 — Parallel proposal to add a `type="pills"` visual variant to `st.tabs`; same `type`-based styling pattern as this radio cards request.

title: st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.slider` accepts `date`/`datetime` bounds that the frontend cannot represent exactly, and silently snaps them to a different instant instead of reporting the problem. The `int` and `float` paths already validate and raise a helpful `StreamlitAPIException`; the timelike path does not.

Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and held in a JavaScript number on the frontend, so only about **1684-07-28 to 2255-06-05** round-trips exactly. Outside that, precision is lost.

`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py` acknowledges the gap:

```python
elif all_timelikes:
    # No validation yet. TODO: check between 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31
    pass
```

Worth noting the TODO's own target range is wrong — most of `0001`–`9999` is not representable, so validating to those limits would not have fixed it.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st

# Silently accepted, but min_value cannot be represented exactly:
st.slider("historical", min_value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(1700, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1))

# Also silently accepted, both bounds unrepresentable:
st.slider("projection", min_value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(2400, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1))

# Raises a bare OverflowError instead of a StreamlitAPIException:
st.slider("ancient", value=dt.date(1, 1, 1))
```

### Actual Behavior

Inspecting the serialized proto shows the bounds exceeding JavaScript's `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with no error raised:

```
in-range 1900..2000      -> NO ERROR. min=-2208988800000000 max=946684800000000  JS-unsafe: none
historical 1600..1700    -> NO ERROR. min=-11676096000000000                      JS-unsafe: ['min']
far future 2300..2400    -> NO ERROR. min=10413792000000000 max=13569465600000000 JS-unsafe: ['min', 'max']
min date 0001..0002      -> OverflowError: date value out of range
```

Two distinct problems:

1. **Moderately out-of-range values are accepted and lose precision.** Years like 1600 or 2300 are ordinary in historical datasets and long-range projections, so this is not just an exotic edge case.
2. **Extreme values raise a bare `OverflowError`.** It comes from `prepared_value[0] - timedelta(days=14)`, which computes the *default* `min_value`/`max_value` even when the caller supplied both explicitly, and overflows next to `date.min`/`date.max`. This is not a `StreamlitAPIException`, so it surfaces as an unhandled Python error rather than actionable guidance.

### Expected Behavior

Out-of-range timelike bounds should raise a `StreamlitAPIException` naming the representable range, matching how the int and float paths already behave. Extreme values should produce that same message rather than an `OverflowError`.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (reproduced at `f2648d7237`)
- Python version: 3.14.5
- OS: macOS 15.5

### Additional Information

Contrast with the existing int path, which is what the timelike path should mirror:

```
`max_value` (9007199254740992) must be <= (1 << 53) - 1
```

comments_data.body:
This is a valid bug in `st.slider`'s date/datetime path. Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and sent as JavaScript numbers, which only preserve exact integers within `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (~±2^53, roughly 1684–2255). Int/float sliders already reject out-of-range bounds via `JSNumber.validate_*_bounds`, but the timelike branch is explicitly a no-op (`# No validation yet`), so moderately out-of-range dates are accepted and silently lose precision. Separately, default `min_value`/`max_value` are always computed as `value ± timedelta(days=14)` before checking whether the caller supplied bounds, which raises a bare `OverflowError` near `date.min`/`date.max` instead of a `StreamlitAPIException`. Fixing this should validate the microsecond form against JS safe-integer limits (not the incorrect 0001–9999 TODO range) and avoid computing unused default bounds that can overflow.

### Related Issues

- [#7427](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7427) — `st.date_input` overflows when computing default selectable bounds near `datetime.max` (similar “default range buffer overflows date extrema” pattern; different widget).
- [#5099](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5099) — `st.slider` bounds-validation inconsistency vs `st.number_input` when `value` is outside `min`/`max` (related to slider bound checking, but not about JS safe-integer / date precision).

No duplicate found for silent JS-precision loss on date/datetime `st.slider` values.

title: Deduplicate identical `st.cache_data` return values to save memory
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.cache_data` stores one serialized (pickled) blob per cache key, where the key is derived only from the function + input arguments. If a function returns the *same* value (e.g. the same dataframe) for many different inputs, each of those cache entries stores a full, redundant copy. We could recognize identical serialized return values (e.g. by hashing the serialized value bytes) and store the payload only once, with each cache key referencing it — saving memory (and disk when persisted).

### Why?

- **Memory savings:** Functions that frequently return the same object under different arguments currently blow up memory with duplicate copies. Content-addressed storage would keep a single shared copy.
- Could also help mitigate memory issues when replaying widgets in cached functions (a common source of memory crashes), since the shared thing would be the stored bytes.
- Complements existing cache memory work like #2911 (limit cache size by memory footprint) and #14558 (inspect cache memory usage).

### How?

Introduce a content-addressed layer for cached values:

- On write, hash the serialized **value payload** and store it once in a blob store keyed by that digest; the per-argument cache key stores a lightweight reference (digest + metadata) plus a reference count.
- On read, resolve the reference to the shared blob and deserialize as usual.
- Evict a blob only when no cache key references it anymore.

Key implementation note: today the pickled entry is a `CachedResult` that bundles the value **and** per-call metadata (replayed `messages`, `main_id`/`sidebar_id`, `stored_at`). Because that metadata differs per key, hashing the whole `CachedResult` blob wouldn't dedup much — the design should **separate the value payload (content-addressable, shared) from the per-key metadata** so identical values actually collide.

Notes:
- Copy semantics are preserved: `st.cache_data` still returns independent copies on each read (values are deserialized per call); only the *stored bytes* are shared.
- Likely only worth it above a size threshold, given the hashing/bookkeeping overhead.

### Additional Context

Current behavior (from a code investigation): storage keys are built from input args only (`_make_value_key`), the return value is `pickle.dumps(CachedResult(...))` and written via `storage.set(value_key, bytes)`, and the in-memory layer is a `TTLCache[str, bytes]` with one independent blob per key. There is no hashing of the return-value bytes and no cross-key dedup today (the only "dedup" in the caching code is background-refresh scheduling).

- Related: #2911 (limit cache by memory footprint), #14558 (inspect cache memory usage), #13992 (cache observability).

title: Add a button group widget with trigger (click) mode
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a button group that supports **trigger (click) mode** instead of selection mode — i.e. a horizontal group of buttons that returns the clicked value once (like `st.button`) and clears after the rerun, rather than persisting a selection. This can either be a new `st.button_group` command or an extension of the existing `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`.

### Why?

It's currently a bit complicated to build things like quick selections / quick replies for chat UIs (a major need for LLM-powered apps), button toolbars, dialog action rows (Confirm / Cancel / Clear), or clickable example grids. Today you have to combine many individual `st.button`s across `st.columns`, which is a lot of boilerplate and looks messy because wrapping depends on each button's label length.

### How?

Two main options:

**Option 1 — Extend `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` with a trigger mode:**

```python
st.pills(..., selection_mode="single" | "multi" | "trigger")
```

In `trigger` mode the widget doesn't keep state: it returns the clicked value and clears it after the rerun (like a button), returning `None` otherwise. `default` wouldn't be allowed in this mode.

**Option 2 — Add a dedicated `st.button_group` command (preferred):**

```python
st.button_group(
    options,
    *,
    format_func=None,
    key=None,
    on_click=None,
    args=None,
    kwargs=None,
    disabled=False,
    type="default" | "rounded",
    wrap=True,
)
```

Behaves like `st.pills` but tailored for triggers: no top label/help (not needed for quick selections), `on_click` instead of `on_change` (aligns with `st.button`), a `type` option for a rounded pill-like look, and a `wrap` option. Keeping triggers in a separate command avoids overloading the selection API (e.g. `selection_mode="trigger"` reads oddly, `default` becomes incompatible, and typing gets awkward).

### Additional Context

- Related: #8318 (quick replies/suggestions for chat responses) — one of the primary motivating use cases.
- Other use cases: button toolbars, dialog action rows, and clickable example grids.

comments_data.body:
This is an enhancement request for a **trigger-mode button group**: a horizontal set of options that behaves like `st.button` (returns the clicked value once, then clears) rather than like `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` (persistent selection). The preferred shape is a dedicated `st.button_group` API; an alternative is extending `selection_mode` with `"trigger"`. Today, workarounds require many `st.button`s in `st.columns`, which is boilerplate-heavy and wraps poorly. Internally, `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` already share `button_group.py` with only `single`/`multi` click modes, so this would either add a third click mode or a thin trigger-oriented public command on that shared implementation.

### Related Issues

- [#8318 – Quick replies/suggestions for chat user response](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8318): Explicitly cited in the issue; a primary motivating use case (suggestion chips / quick replies) that a trigger-mode button group would enable.
- [#10740 – Add a configurable toolbar or clickable actions to `st.chat_message`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10740): Related chat UI need for clickable action rows; a trigger button group could be a building block for message-level actions.
- [#16240 – Add a stateful button](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16240): Complementary button-semantics proposal (persistent toggle-styled button vs. this issue’s ephemeral click group); not a duplicate, but adjacent API design.

body:

### Summary

Add a native command menu / command palette widget that opens with a keyboard shortcut (e.g. `Cmd/Ctrl+K`) and lets users quickly search and trigger app-defined commands. Similar to the [`cmdk`](https://uiw.tf/cmdk) React component and the command palettes found in VS Code, Linear, Raycast, etc.

### Why?

Command palettes are a fast, keyboard-first way to navigate and act in an app — jumping between pages, running actions, changing settings, or searching. For data apps and internal tools with many pages/actions, this is a big UX and power-user win, and it's currently only achievable with custom components.

### How?

A widget that registers a searchable list of commands and opens as an overlay on `Cmd/Ctrl+K` (and/or programmatically). Rough sketch:

```python
choice = st.command_menu(
    [
        {"label": "Go to Dashboard", "icon": ":material/dashboard:", "group": "Navigation"},
        {"label": "Export data", "icon": ":material/download:", "group": "Actions"},
    ],
    placeholder="Type a command or search...",
)
if choice == "Export data":
    ...
```

Possible features:
- Fuzzy search, grouping/sections, icons, keyboard navigation.
- Customizable trigger shortcut and a programmatic open.
- Returns the selected command (rerun-based), similar to other widgets.
- Optionally integrate with multipage navigation (pages appear as commands automatically).

### Additional Context

- Prior art: [`cmdk`](https://uiw.tf/cmdk) (fast, composable command menu for React).

### Why?

Displaying 3D models is a common need for CAD, scientific/medical visualization, product/asset previews, ML/3D reconstruction outputs, and gaming. Today users rely on the streamlit-extras component or custom components, which is extra setup and not officially maintained. A first-class element would make 3D viewing a one-liner and keep it maintained in-sync with Streamlit.

### How?

A new command, e.g. `st.model_viewer` / `st.three_viewer`, roughly mirroring the streamlit-extras API:

```python
st.model_viewer("model.glb")
st.model_viewer("https://example.com/model.gltf", height=600)
st.model_viewer(stl_bytes, file_format=".stl")
```

Parameters (to be refined):
- `source`: URL, local path, `bytes`, or file-like object.
- `file_format`: optional explicit format override (inferred otherwise).
- `height`: viewer height in pixels.
- `key`: widget key.

Supported formats: GLTF/GLB (recommended), OBJ, STL, PLY, FBX. Could later add options for background, camera, lighting, and auto-rotate.

title: Allow prepending/appending text (prefix/suffix addons) to `st.text_input`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Allow prepending and appending static text to `st.text_input` (input-group-style "addons"), e.g. a `https://` prefix, an `@gmail.com` suffix, or a unit like `kg`. This is already partly covered by the `icon` parameter, but that only supports an icon, not arbitrary text.

### Why?

Prefix/suffix addons are a very common form pattern (URLs, usernames, currencies, units, domains). Today users either build custom components or hack it together with adjacent columns/markdown, which doesn't look integrated and misaligns with the input. Native support would make forms cleaner and more professional with minimal effort.

### How?

Add optional parameters to prepend/append text to the input, rendered as attached addons inside/adjacent to the input field. For example:

```python
st.text_input("Website", prefix="https://")
st.text_input("Email", suffix="@gmail.com")
st.text_input("Weight", suffix="kg")
```

Naming TBD (e.g. `prefix`/`suffix` vs `prepend`/`append`). The added text is display-only and not part of the widget's returned value. Could build on the existing `icon` addon slot.

### Additional Context

- Partly covered today by the `icon` parameter of `st.text_input`.
- Related: #6704 (specialized input types for `st.text_input`).

title: Server-side validation of client-side widget constraints
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Widget constraints like `options` allow-lists, `disabled`, `num_rows`, `max_chars`, and DataFrame column `validate` are enforced only in the browser, so a forged `WidgetState`/`BackMsg` can submit out-of-constraint values that flow into `st.session_state`, callbacks, and return values. We could add a way to have Streamlit re-check these constraints server-side.


### Why?

Many developers reasonably assume `st.selectbox(options=[...])` can only return one of its options, or that `disabled=True` blocks a value/callback — but that only holds client-side. Relying on it today means hand-rolling server-side validation for every widget, which is easy to forget.

### How?

Enforce declared widget constraints server-side by default in the widget deserialize path — validating the incoming value against `options` allow-lists, `min_value`/`max_value`, `max_chars`, `disabled=True`, and `st.data_editor` `disabled`/`num_rows`/column `validate`. On a violation, coerce to a valid value (reset to default / clamp), consistent with how Streamlit already handles stale `options` today, so normal frontend/backend sync races don't break.

### Additional Context

### Summary

In the sidebar when st.selectbox sits near the bottom, the component opens its dropdown downward and the options overflow past the bottom of the viewport instead of flipping upward. This changed between 1.58 and 1.59/1.60: in 1.58 the same app flips the dropdown upward so it stays on screen; in 1.59 it opens downward and overflows. This issue only occurs in the sidebar.

Observed rendered DOM difference (offered as evidence): in 1.58 the open listbox renders at the document root as a sibling of #portal (ul[data-testid="stSelectboxVirtualDropdown"]), so its placement is viewport-relative and it flips. In 1.59 the widget is a react-aria-ComboBox and the open listbox renders inside [data-testid="stSidebar"], which is position: relative, so it is anchored to the sidebar and opens downward only.

import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(layout="wide")

with st.sidebar:

st.title("Streamlit Dropdown Demo")

title: Add `allowed_dates` parameter to st.date_input to restrict selectable dates to a specific list
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, st.date_input only supports continuous date ranges via min_value and max_value. 
There is no way to restrict selectable dates to a specific list of valid dates, such as 
dates available in a dataframe. Adding an allowed_dates parameter would fill this gap.

### Why?

I'm always frustrated when I need to show a date picker that only allows the user to select 
dates that exist in a dataset. For example, when a dataframe contains sales data only for 
specific dates, the current widget allows the user to select any date in the range, even 
dates with no data. This forces developers to use workarounds like st.selectbox, which 
lacks the calendar UI and date-picking experience that st.date_input provides.

### How?

Introduce a new parameter called `allowed_dates` in `st.date_input` with the following behavior:

- Accepts a list of datetime.date objects
- Disables all dates not present in the list in the calendar UI
- Example usage:

import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"date": ["2025-01-01", "2025-01-15", "2025-02-10"]})
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"]).dt.date

selected = st.date_input(
    "Select a date",
    allowed_dates=df["date"].tolist()
)

### Additional Context

This feature request was inspired by a common use case discussed while using st.date_input  with dataframes. The current workaround is to use st.selectbox with the list of available dates, but this sacrifices the calendar UI   experience.

Related issue: st.date_input currently supports min_value and max_value for continuous 
ranges, but has no support for non-continuous date lists.

title: Widgets in an st.popover opened inside an st.dialog are occluded by the dialog and unusable
body:
### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When an `st.popover` is used inside an `st.dialog`, the popover opens but its body
is rendered underneath the dialog's interaction layer. Widgets inside the popover
(e.g. a `selectbox`) cannot be interacted with, and clicking them lands on the
dialog's dismissable overlay — which can close the dialog. This is a regression
from the migration of `st.dialog` to React Aria (#15327); it worked in 1.58.0.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st


@st.dialog("My dialog")
def show_dialog():
    st.write("dialog content")
    with st.popover("Open popover"):
        fruit = st.selectbox("Fruit", ["Apple", "Banana", "Cherry"])
        st.write(f"picked: {fruit}")


if st.button("Open dialog"):
    show_dialog()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and click **Open dialog**.
2. Inside the dialog, click **Open popover** (the popover body appears).
3. Try to open the popover's `selectbox` dropdown and pick an option.
4. The dropdown does not open; clicking in the popover body instead hits the
   dialog overlay (and can dismiss the dialog).

### Expected Behavior

The popover body renders above the dialog and its widgets are fully interactive:
opening the `selectbox`, picking an option, and having the value commit —
dismissing neither the popover nor the dialog. (This is how it behaved in 1.58.0.)

### Current Behavior

The popover body is occluded by the dialog. The in-popover widget is not
interactable, and interacting with it can close the dialog.

Objective evidence (Playwright, both Chromium and WebKit): hit-testing the
in-popover selectbox at its own center with `document.elementFromPoint` returns
the dialog rather than the widget, and the dropdown cannot be opened even with a
forced click:

```
selectbox_hit = { topTestId: "stDialog", inBody: false, inDialog: true }
dropdown_opened = false
```

Root cause: the popover body is portalled to `document.body` (outside the dialog's
DOM subtree), while `st.dialog` is now a React Aria (`data-rac`) overlay that
establishes its own stacking/overlay layer that paints and hit-tests above the
portalled popover body. Control: a BaseWeb overlay opened from a widget placed
**directly** in the dialog (e.g. a `multiselect` in the dialog) renders correctly
above the dialog, so the dialog does not occlude all portalled overlays — only the
popover body at the `popup` z-tier.

### Is this a regression?
- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Confirmed via `git bisect` (probe: is the in-popover selectbox usable above the
dialog?):

| Commit | Description | Result |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| tag `1.58.0` (`209ad55c`) | 1.58.0 release (does not contain #15327) | PASS |
| `590deca9` | parent of #15327 | PASS |
| **`a7200715` (#15327)** | **Remove `BaseWeb` for `Dialog` (React Aria migration)** | **FAIL (first bad commit)** |
| `d65a3aae` (#15339) | Remove BaseWeb for Popover (floating-ui) | FAIL (not the cause) |
| current `develop` | — | FAIL |

#15327 shipped in 1.59.0 and is not in 1.58.0, which is why 1.58.0 works and
1.59.0+ is broken. This is independent of the `st.popover` floating-ui migration
(#15339). There is a prior related fix, #15876 "Fix React Aria dialog overlay
stacking", which does not cover this popover-in-dialog case.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (reproduces on 1.59.0 and later; first broken in #15327)
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chromium and WebKit (both affected)

### Additional Information

- Scope: only the combination **popover inside a dialog** is affected. Standalone
  popovers, and widgets placed directly in a dialog, work correctly.
- Suggested direction for a fix: render/portal the popover body into the dialog's
  overlay/stacking context when it is opened inside a dialog, or raise the popover
  body to a tier that clears the React Aria dialog overlay (mirroring how direct
  BaseWeb overlays clear it via the `basewebOverlay` tier).
- Found during QA of PR #15961 (which fixes the separate #15959 popover-overlay
  stacking/dismissal issues). This popover-in-dialog gap is not caused by, and is
  out of scope for, that PR.

### Summary

**Regression in 1.59.0** (1.58.0 is fine): when a widget inside an `st.tabs` tab triggers a rerun, the tab bar disappears and the content of **all** tabs renders stacked vertically down the page, as if the tabs container no longer exists. A browser reload restores the tabs until the next widget interaction.

Possibly related to the tabs DOM rework in 1.59.0: in 1.58.0 each tab renders a `[data-baseweb="tab-panel"]` element (4 tabs → 4 panels, 1 visible); in 1.59.0 those elements are gone entirely.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.title("Tabs regression repro")

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
df = pd.DataFrame({"x": range(20), "y": rng.rand(20)})


def tab_content(name: str) -> None:
    st.metric("Metric", name)
    st.dataframe(df.head(3))
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df).mark_bar().encode(x="x:O", y="y:Q"), use_container_width=True)
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df).mark_line().encode(x="x:O", y="y:Q"), use_container_width=True)
    st.subheader("Leaderboard")
    choice = st.selectbox("Date range", ["A", "B", "C"], key=f"{name}_sel")
    n = {"A": 5, "B": 10, "C": 15}[choice]
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df.head(n)).mark_bar().encode(x="y:Q", y="x:O"), use_container_width=True)


names = ["All", "Indy", "Clarksville", "Fort Wayne"]
for tab, name in zip(st.tabs(names), names):
    with tab:
        tab_content(name)
```

### Steps To Reproduce
